A key point is that host and loaded layers have different symmetry, which enables effective control of symmetry-related properties in topological photonics and non-Hermitian photonics. We show two examples: phase-change material, GST-loaded photonic crystal for topological phase transition induced by the material phase transition, and graphene-loaded photonic crystals for manipulating exceptional points and non-Hermitian chiral properties.

articleTitle: SiP Ring Resonator Modulator-based Transmitters for Short-Reach Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Silicon photonics (SiP) is a key enabling technology for high-symbol rate communication to enable future 800 Gbps and 1.6 Tbps solutions in scalable and energy efficiency way. The 800G pluggable multi-source agreement (MSA) suggests that intensity-modulated direct-detection (IM/DD) is the most sustainable way forward [1]. Recent advances [2–12] in SiP enable dense integration, high yield, and low energy consumption for optical interconnects. Monolithic integration of SiP and complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) eliminates need of additional packaging and integration allowing to introduce compact arrayed waveguide grating routers [2] or extremely efficient wavelength division multiplexing filters [3]. All silicon avalanche photodiode [4] has demonstrated $0.73 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{W}$, and more than 38 GHz RF bandwidth in O-band operation. To ensure high symbol rate operation high operational bandwidth of each transceiver component is necessary. High-bandwidth SiP slow light modulator [5] and wide free spectral range SiP ring resonator modulator (RRM) [6] have been demonstrated. On-off keying (OOK) at highest symbol rate should be considered thanks to high energy efficiency and simple driving electronics. At expense of more complex driver electronics pulse amplitude modulation with 4 levels also can be considered if the modulator extinction ratio supports it. SiP RRM have unique advantages as low power consumption, small footprint, high scalability, suitability for multichannel operation and easier integration with CMOS drivers and electronics. Recently SiP RRM was used to demonstrate 160 Gbaud OOK [7]. SiP RRM with integrated laser demonstrated 128 Gbaud OOK/PAM4 [8]. Multichannel integration advantages of SiP RRM have been shown by implementing $4 \times 112 \mathrm{Gbps}$ [9], $4 \times 224 \mathrm{Gbps}$ [10] and $16 \times 56 \mathrm{Gbps}$ [11] in O-band as well $32 \times 16 \mathrm{Gbps}$ [12] in C-band. In this paper, we report on several SiP RRM-based transmitters to achieve high symbol rate with performance below 6.7% overhead (OH) hard-decision forward error correction (HD-FEC) threshold of $4.5 \times 10^{-3}$ [13]. We demonstrate on-off keying (OOK) transmission for optical-back-to-back and after transmission over 100 meters of single mode fiber (SMF). RRMs are characterized with [14].

articleTitle: Optical Screening System Using Biospeckle Imaging and Texture-Based Analysis for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is a prevalent cause of cancerrelated mortality in women, posing a significant public health challenge that demands effective screening techniques for cancer detection. To address this need, biospeckle imaging, as a non-destructive and cost-efficient method, has emerged to assess the functionality and activity of biological tissues. However, it is necessary to investigate algorithms capable of interpreting and analyzing biospeckle patterns susceptible by experimental conditions. In this investigation, a novel optical screening system utilizing biospeckle imaging for breast cancer screening is proposed, incorporating a promising texture-based multi-neighborhood local entropy analysis. The biospeckle patterns are generated from samples of human breast tissue. The analysis approach extracts histogram-based features from texture maps to capture spatial intensity and phase variations of biospeckle patterns associated with breast tissue functionality. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) is employed to identify the most informative features. By employing a nonlinear support vector machine (SVM) algorithm, the relationship between the selected features and breast conditions is established. The proposed method introduces a viable imaging system for BC prediction, achieving a maximum accuracy and recall of $97.29 \%$, precision of $98.05 \%$, and $F 1$ score of $97.98 \%$.

articleTitle: Towards high-resolution all-optical spatial light modulators
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Spatial light modulators are currently used to shape wavefronts at micron scales for various applications such as lighting, beam steering or digital holography. High-resolution holographic displays require the smallest pixels. Today, liquid crystal on silicon (LCOS) technology does not allow pixel pitch to be reduced to less than 1 μm, and metasurface technology still does not allow independent control of each meta-atom in the visible range. With this in mind, we turned our attention to a new all-optical addressing principle based on crossed silicon waveguides coupled to plasmonic nanoparticles (NPs), themselves interacting with a phase-change material. We will describe the various steps involved in demonstrating this system, with the aim of achieving a high-resolution, all-optical spatial light modulator.

articleTitle: LCOS-based Flexible Optical Switch for Heterogeneous SDM Fiber Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this study, we present a novel LCOS-based flexible optical switch specifically designed for heterogeneous spatial division multiplexing (SDM) fiber networks. This switch offers seamless connectivity between various types of SDM fibers, eliminating the need for Fan-In and Fan-Out (FIFO) devices. To evaluate the efficacy of the proposed switch, we performed extensive measurements on the optical insertion loss and crosstalk characteristics on the full C-band. The results validate the concept of the flexible optical switch and demonstrate the feasibility of implementing a heterogeneous SDM fiber network using simple optical devices.

articleTitle: Quantum information and Artificial Neural Networks-based Signal Processing using Integrated Photonics
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Integrated photonics is contributing to new emerging technologies for advanced signal processing, based on machine learning and quantum information science. In this work, we utilize compact, reconfigurable, on-chip devices to develop photonic artificial neural networks and quantum signal processors for telecommunication applications. Our work demonstrates the recovery and reconstruction of high-speed telecommunication signals with ultralow latency, as well as enhances the speed and security of quantum communication. Characterized by their highly efficient and intelligent processing, parallelization, and reduced power consumption, these technologies are set to pave the way for the next generation of telecom networks.

articleTitle: CV-QKD in Coexistence with 1 Gb/s Classical Channel Using Electrical Frequency Division Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to enable secure secret key exchange. Continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD), utilizing coherent states and coherent detection, has emerged as a promising method, easily integrable into existing telecom networks. In this work, we study, through numerical simulation, the coexistence of a CV-QKD channel with a classical channel capable of up to 1 Gb/s. We first analyze the performance of the quantum channel when the classical channel emits a pure tone, by varying the frequency gap between both channels and adjusting their power ratios. Then, by maintaining a fixed electrical separation of 500 MHz, we study QPSK modulation with root-raised-cosine filtering in the classical channel. In this scenario, for several signal-to-noise ratios, we reduce crosstalk by optimizing filter properties such as roll-off factor, symbol rate and number of filter taps.

articleTitle: Extraordinary enhancement of Second harmonic generation in cavity-resonator integrated grating couplers
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Cavity resonator integrated grating filters (CRIGF) [1] are composed with a sub-wavelength coupling grating of a few tens of periods (GC), surrounded with two distributed Bragg reflectors (DBR), etched on a multilayer stack of lossless dielectric materials (see Fig. 1). Illuminated with an incident beam overlying the GC, CRIGF exhibit resonances characterised by a strong electromagnetic field concentrated in the guiding layer beneath the structuration. We are currently exploiting this property to enhance second order nonlinear optical effects, in particular second harmonic generation (SHG) [2]. The main applications targeted in the long term are efficient and compact optical sources in wavelength ranges where technological solutions are rare. For this exploratory work, we are interested in the conversion from $1.55 \mu \mathrm{m}$ to 775nm.

articleTitle: On the Control of Multi-Function Reprogrammable Silicon Chip for ROADMs and Sliceable Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This study investigates the use of a reconfigurable multi-functional reprogrammable silicon chip as an add/drop network device for a sliceable bandwidth variable transceiver. Software-Defined Networking (SDN) with NETCONF/YANG protocol is used for control and management, leveraging REST API to facilitate communication and coordination between the device local controller and the silicon chip-integrated device.

articleTitle: Squeezed light photon number statistics from a microresonator without photon number resolving detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Measuring the photon number distribution (PND) of optical states allows one to extract metrics of non-classicality of fundamental and technological relevance, but requires in principle the use of detectors with photon number resolving capabilities (PNR). Here we reconstruct the PND of two-mode pulsed squeezed light generated from a silicon nitride microresonator using threshold detectors and variable optical attenuations. The PNDs are characterized up to $\sim 1.2$ photons/pulse, corresponding to an on-chip squeezing level of $6.2(2) \ \mathrm{dB}$ and a noise reduction factor (photon number difference squeezing) of $3.8(2) \ \mathrm{dB}$. The analysis performed on the photon-number basis allows us to additionally characterize the influence of a spurious thermal background field that reduces the photon number correlations.

articleTitle: Integrated photonic crystal nanotweezers for bacteria and bacteriophages viruses trapping and susceptibility testing
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a major threat to public health. This resistance is due to multiple factors such as natural bacterial mutations, but above all to the overuse of antibiotics in agronomic and medical practices. Traditional antimicrobial susceptibility testing relies on time-consuming bacterial growth processes. We will present the results of a new method enabling antibiotic or phage susceptibility testing with single phages or bacteria trapped in an optical chip. The system used is a photonic chip containing hollow photonic crystal cavities topped by a microfluidic system for transporting bacteria and phages. We will present the optical signature of bacterial and phage trapping in the transmitted light that excites the optical trap. This makes it possible to distinguish between different phage families, as well as the level of stress or death of a single bacterium in the presence of antibiotics or phages.

articleTitle: Service Function Chain Resource Allocation and Offloading in Constrained Edge-Cloud Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Internet Service Providers (ISPs) face escalating data traffic and diverse application needs, prompting the adoption of 5 G technology to enhance network agility and intelligence. However, traditional networks fall short, necessitating the integration of Network Function Virtualization (NFV), Software-Defined Networking (SDN), and Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC). Despite advancements, efficient resource allocation remains a challenge, especially with edge computing. This study evaluates Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and Heuristic algorithms for Virtual Network Embedding (VNE) in 5G networks. Results provide insights into optimal resource allocation and offloading strategies.

articleTitle: Visible-light modulators and power limiters based on spin crossover material thin films
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We review our recent studies on visible-light modulators exploiting a relatively uncommon yet attractive family of phase change materials, the spin crossover molecular complexes. In particular, we report different embodiments, based on thermally-activated thin films of the evaporable iron 1,2,4,-triazolyl borate compound, that have been successively designed and fabricated to obtain proof-of-principle demonstrators but also devices with enhanced modulation depth and spectral bandwidth. We show that the response of the components can be affected by self-heating, leading in turn to optical power limiting behaviour.

articleTitle: Thin Film Lithium Niobate 1xN Multimode Interference Splitters
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of different configurations of 1 xN multimode interference (MMI) splitters made of thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguides. The proposed 1xN MMI beam splitters allow the connection between 1 input and N outputs with a single device, without the need of cascading multiple components. It is shown that the different output ports of the designed 1 xN MMI splitters (i.e. with $\mathrm{N}=3,5$, 7) exhibit a good uniformity of power at the N outputs (less than 0.71 dB for the worst case ($\mathrm{N}=7$)) and a constant phase shift, which is stable in the whole considered wavelength range. Moreover, the overall insertion loss for different number N of outputs is less than 0.1 dB at the wavelength $\lambda=1.55 \mu \mathrm{m}$. These performances make the proposed 1 xN MMI splitters promising as feeding components for Optical Phased Array (OPA).

articleTitle: Converged 5G/6G access-metro network combining RoF and coherent PONs
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The deployment of 5G and the anticipated 6G technologies impose novel challenges to existing time division multiplexing-passive optical network (TDM-PON) access infrastructures, requiring stringent QoS. To address this, we propose a hybrid access-metro network with numerous high-density ultra-dense wavelength division multiplexing (udWDM) and radio over fiber (RoF) PONs. There, one type of PON is based on power splitters, using lightpaths with coherent transmissions; while another type, based on arrayed wavelengths gratings (AWGs), supports RoF. Both converge to a metro network through optical nodes. All remote radio heads (RRHs) at base stations connect to a centralized optical line terminal (C-OLT) at the central office (CO), managing a centralized/cloud radio access network (C-RAN). This integrated design provides reconfigurable capabilities, optimizes efficiency and minimizes latency for new wireless technologies.

articleTitle: Cross-Switching of C-Band Pulses in Dual-Core Soft Glass Fibers with Different Measure of Asymmetry
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We present a comprehensive experimental investigation of dual-wavelength switching involving $1560 \mathrm{~nm}, 75 \mathrm{fs}$ pulses (referred to as signal) driven by $1030 \mathrm{~nm}, 270 \mathrm{fs}$ pulses (referred to as control) using two high index contrast dual-core fibers with different measure of dual-core asymmetry. Beside the asymmetry, the study explores the influence of fiber length and control pulse energy on the switching performance. In the case of fiber with higher asymmetry, we achieved an exceptional switching contrast of 41.6 dB at 14 mm fiber length, exhibiting a broadband character within the spectral range of 1450-1650 nm. In contrast, the fiber with lower asymmetry enabled a maximum switching contrast of 10.7 dB at 22 mm fiber length. According to our understanding the switching mechanism is driven by nonlinear balancing of dual-core asymmetry, therefore it took place at lower control pulse energy in the latter case. Our findings underscore the critical role of proper dual-core asymmetry in achieving efficient switching performance and have significant potential applications.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic-Maxwell approach to light-matter interactions at the nanoscale: High Harmonic generation in Silicon
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The last few years have witnessed significant development in the study of linear and nonlinear optical properties of materials at the nanoscale. This includes metals, semiconductors, conductive oxides, and more recently, time varying media. More often than not, experimental results are reported without the benefit of rigorous theoretical models. I will present a basic hydrodynamic Maxwell approach that can be used to take into account and simulate all relevant light-matter interactions, depending on the circumstances. For example, simulations in the time domain and in the ultrafast regime can simultaneously account for surface and magnetic nonlinearities, linear and nonlinear nonlocal effects, linear and nonlinear material dispersions beyond the third order, and a phase locking mechanism that makes high harmonic generation possible for semiconductors like silicon deep in the UV range.

articleTitle: Comprehensive comparison between versions CVSS v2.0, CVSS v3.x and CVSS v4.0 as vulnerability severity measures
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper, presents a comparative study for three versions of Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS), CVSS v2.0, CVSS v3.x and newest CVSS v4.0. The focus is laid on new metrics added in CVSS v4.0, i.e. Threat Metrics, Impact Metrics exceeding Confidentiality (C), Integrity (I), and Availability (A), and optional Supplemental Metrics providing additional information regarding security, and automated approach towards environment assessment using assets databases. Concluded research showed a more defined approach in the newest standard, defining Base $(B)$, Threat $(T)$ and Environmental $(E)$ metrics components as part of the CVSS assessment. Python and NodeJs applications were developed to calculate the CVSS scores. The analysis is further supported by a qualitative study of selected vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: High-quality factor microsphere as sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Whispering gallery mode (WGM) microspheres have gained prominence as sensors in various applications due to their ability to significantly enhance light-matter interaction. In fact, the sensitivity of these sensors is directly correlated with their quality factor (Q), and melted glass microspheres typically exhibit a Q-factor of approximately $10^{5}$ when used as sensors (functionalized and/or in the measurement environment). Usually, the predominant sensing mechanism involves monitoring mode shifts, where the resonant wavelength of the WGM is employed to measure the desired signal. However, at higher Q-factors, characterized by narrower bandwidths, sophisticated equipment is required for accurate measurements. In this study, we utilize an active microsphere as a sensor with an exceptional Q-factor exceeding $10^{8}$ in the measurement environment, thanks to its gain. We opt for an alternative sensing mechanism that leverages the microsphere’s gain to measure the signal of interest. Lastly, we compare this innovative sensing approach with other techniques commonly employed in optical sensors based on WGM micro resonators.

articleTitle: Indium Fluoride Optical Fiber End-Pump Combiner for High-Power All-Fiber Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this paper, tapering and splicing techniques for optical fibers based on fluoride glass are illustrated, valuable for the next generation of all-fiber lasers emitting in the mid-infrared spectral range. In particular, a 5×1 optical fiber combiner is fabricated via stretching and heating technique. The performance of the device is assessed via superluminescent diode emitting around the wavelength $\lambda=1.55 \mu \mathrm{m}$. The splicing of two fluoride optical fibers is also investigated, due to the need to splice the output port of the 5×1 optical fiber combiner with a rare-earth doped optical fiber.

articleTitle: Phase Noise Reduction in Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution Using Digital Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables information-theoretic-secure secret key exchange thanks to the laws of quantum mechanics. Since it can easily be incorporated into existing telecom networks, continuous-variable QKD (CV QKD) using coherent states and coherent detection has recently emerged as a promising candidate. However, the secret key rate and link distance in CV QKD systems are still limited by the imperfections of used components. In this work, through simulations, we study the use of different digital filtering techniques for optical phase recovery, aided by pilot symbols, to mitigate the phase noise induced by the coherent mixing of two free-running lasers in a CV QKD system. Moving average, Butterworth and unscented Kalman filters are evaluated for different phase drift conditions. Results show that phase recovery from small amplitude pilot symbols, along with further digital filtering, can considerably reduce phase noise and measurement error, while increasing the secret key rate and link distance of the CV QKD system.

articleTitle: Buried Heterostructure InAs/InP Quantum Dash Lasers at 1.3 μm
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this paper, we report for the first time, to the best of our knowledge, on buried heterostructure InAs quantum dash (QDash) lasers on InP substrate emitting at 1.3 μm. An optimized growth process was developed on our state-of-the-art gas-source molecular beam epitaxy reactor, enabling the formation of high-density QDashes on InP(100) substrate exhibiting a narrow photoluminescence full-width at half maximum (FWHM) of 68.1 nm (49 meV) at 300 K. Single transverse mode buried heterostructure Fabry-Pérot lasers were fabricated using our well-established buried ridge stripe process. The lasers exhibit low threshold currents, round optical mode with 12° x 13° FWHM beam divergence, flat emission spectrum and spontaneous mode-locking with longitudinal modes beating linewidths down to 30 kHz. These results demonstrate the capability of InAs/InP QDashes to address applications in the telecom O-band, extending the spectral coverage allowed by this material system.

articleTitle: Impact of Waveband and Wavelength Switching in the Next-Generation Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The rapid and significant increase in Internet traffic, driven by developments in 5G/6G mobile communications, video streaming, cloud computing, and other high-bandwidth applications, challenges the capabilities of existing optical network infrastructures. This progress necessitates the creation of optical networks that can be expanded, have large capacity, and are affordable. This article evaluates the performance of a new multi-band optical cross-connect (OXC) architecture that uses waveband (WB) switching technologies at the network level. WB switching, a technique that combines many wavelengths into larger bands for more efficient routing, is a potential solution to overcome future optical networks’ scalability and complexity issues. WB switching streamlines network design and decreases operating costs by decreasing the number of necessary switching components, in contrast to standard wavelength (WL) switching, which treats each wavelength as a separate route. Our study, using extensive simulation evaluations, demonstrates the possibility of this design to provide the extensive parallelism and bandwidth capacity required for next-generation bandwidth-intensive optical networks. The results suggest that WB switching can greatly improve network performance by providing a simplified yet effective method for managing increasing data traffic. This represents a feasible way to achieve bandwidth-rich and highly parallel optical networks for the 6G era and beyond. This contribution establishes the foundation for future studies on enhancing optical network designs to address the increasing requirements of global communication without going into the details of routing and spectrum assignment schemes.

articleTitle: Investigation of Spontaneous Raman Scattering in Combined Classical and Quantum Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Including Quantum Key Distribution service into classical high-speed optical data transmission networks applying a dense wavelength division multiplexing technique via one joint fibre is a cost-effective solution to improve the network’s security. Several noise sources degrade the quality of the quantum channel in this multichannel system. Optical filtering cannot eliminate the optical nonlinear effects, like Spontaneous Raman Scattering caused by the classical optical channels. The paper thoroughly investigates this nonlinear optical effect with different combined classical and quantum system topologies. The applied model uses experimental values of Spontaneous Raman Scattering.

articleTitle: Optical response of electric memristive systems
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Memristive devices are physically reconfigurable systems whose resistance state is intricately tied to the history of applied voltage and current. This functionality is achieved by manipulating ion distribution within a solid-state film, allowing for the modification of its electrical properties in a non-volatile but reversible manner. As their characteristics cannot be replicated by any combination of fundamental resistors, capacitors, or inductors, it is believed that in the future, memristors may lead to the development of new intelligent and efficient computing systems. However, the next step in memristor evolution is to introduce light in optoelectronic memristor systems. Optical signals offer several advantages over electrical inputs, including high bandwidth, reduced power consumption, minimal crosstalk, and negligible resistance-capacitance delay. Here, we explore the performance of the metal-dielectric-metal memristive device using ellipsometric measurements. We demonstrate how the applied voltage influences not only the system’s resistance state but also the optical signal. The study underscores the distinct characteristics observed in electrical and optical changes within the device.

articleTitle: MIMO DSP in Direct Detection SDM Systems Based on Weakly-Coupled Multicore Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper explores a new class of space-division-multiplexing (SDM) optical communication links based on weakly-coupled multicore fibers (WC-MCF). These links achieve higher capacity by utilizing WC-MCFs with denser packing of fiber cores. The increased core density leads to significant intercore crosstalk (ICXT), which can no longer be neglected as in WC-MCF links but can be mitigated by a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) digital signal processing (DSP) algorithm. We conducted a numerical study of a passive optical network (PON) link of this new class, which uses a 20 km 8 -core WC-MCF. Our findings show that, when the total ICXT strength is moderate, the MIMO time-domain equalizer (TDE) applied after direct detection (DD) is capable of reducing the mean bit-error ratio (BER) by 1.2 to 2.4 times. Moreover, MIMO TDE significantly lowers the BER in rare but impactful strong-ICXT events that produce high BERs, thus, enhancing the overall link performance and stability.

articleTitle: Quantum imaging with undetected photons
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We present principles of quantum imaging with undetected photons (QIUP) and show modifications we made to the nonlinear interferometer for QUIP in order to use off-axes holography for faster image reconstruction. We present images made by off-axes quantum holography (OAQH) and discuss image capabilities of the system. In this work we use a pair of quantum correlated photons, generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a non-linear crystal; one photon form a pair interacts with object, and another is detected. In our system both photons are in near infra-red, but by slight modifications they will be in different spectral regions, interacting photons in mid infra-red, detected photons in visible or near infra-ed. This opens very useful applications of QIUP for imaging and sensing in MIR.

articleTitle: Proactive Spectrum Assignment for Transient Mitigation in Multi-Band Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In multi-band networks, the problem of power transients due to spectral loading changes (due to link failures and/or channel add/drop) can have considerable impact on surviving traffic relative to standard C-band operation, due to the increased impact of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) effects between co-transmitted bands. In this paper, we evaluate how selectively assigning spectrum in the C - and L-bands according the potential failure profiles in the network can help reduce the average and worst-case effect of power transients due to loading changes. This type of strategy also presents an intricate trade-off, since better transient resiliency allows channels to operate with lower margins (and thus with higher modulation formats), but on the other hand a transient minimization spectrum assignment may lead to increased fragmentation. The comparison will help identify in which types of networks and traffic use-cases these specialized spectrum assignment techniques are most promising.

articleTitle: Glass Photonics: a brilliant successful story
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Glass Photonics has a long and successful history, characterized by a broad spectrum of interdisciplinary scientific domains, involving physicists, chemists, material scientists, engineers, and recently researchers in deep learning and sophisticated models. Glass photonics obtained important outcomes covering the basic science as well as critical applications ICT oriented, lighting, laser, sensing, energy, environment, biological and medical sciences, and quantum technologies Among the important number of photonic glasses outcomes, we will comment on some consolidated and recent results about bulks, waveguides, films, fibers, resonators and metastructures.

articleTitle: Novel 2D Glassy-Graphene for Photodetection and Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Herein we review novel two-dimensional (2D) glassy-graphene that is in an intermediate state between glassy carbon and graphene and that has high crystallinity but curly lattice planes. A polymer-assisted approach is introduced to grow an ultra-smooth (roughness, <0.7 nm) glassy-graphene thin film at the inch scale. Owing to the advantages inherited by the glassy-graphene thin film from graphene and glassy carbon, the glassy-graphene thin film exhibits conductivity, transparency, and flexibility comparable to those of graphene, as well as glassy carbon-like mechanical and chemical stability. Moreover, an intrinsic bandgap arising from the distorted lattice structure enables glassy-graphene to exhibit comparable or even improved photodetection and chemical sensing capability, compared with pristine gapless graphene. Consequently, high-performance and transparent photodetectors based on $\mathrm{MoS}_{2} /$ glassy-graphene heterostructures with high detectivity were fabricated, exhibiting marked improvement of charge transfer and distinct wavelength selectivity. Meanwhile, the vis-NIR photodetection and chemical sensing device is developed based on glassy-graphene that meets similar property requirements. The signal-to-noise-ratio of the multifunctional device for detecting acetone shows more than $50 \%$ improvement over the device based on graphene. Thereby, large scale 2D glassy-graphene thin film has great potential applications in flexible electronics, photonics and chemical sensing.

articleTitle: Interaction of Continuous Waves and Laser Cavity-Solitons in Micro-Resonators: Enhancing Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We explore the nonlinear emergence and recovery of a bonded state consisting of a soliton and a continuous wave (CW), with the soliton being red-detuned and the CW blue-detuned relative to the microcavity resonance slopes. Our findings demonstrate that the blue-detuned CW and soliton form in distinct regions of the erbium laser spectrum, where the slow resonant nonlinearity of the amplifier exhibits a different sign. Real-time measurements using Dispersive Fourier Transform (DFT) reveal an elastic bonding between these states, mediated by the system’s modal structure and slow nonlinearities. This study provides crucial insights into the dynamic interaction of complex laser states and suggests potential enhancements to the stability of solitary regimes.

articleTitle: A simple model for a dye-based solid state random laser
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The wide variety of materials and experimental setups used in solid-state random lasers (SSRLs) makes it difficult to understand the spectro-temporal dynamical complexities exhibited by these devices with a single operational theoretical model. This contribution presents a comparison between a simple theoretical model and the experimental spectro-temporal characteristics of a dye-based solid state random laser (SSRL) operating in the diffusive regime under ultrafast pumping. The random laser is based on a ground powder of a rhodamine B-doped hybrid compound incorporated into a diureasil host. The precise analysis of the time-resolved emission of the SSRL was carried out by developing an experimental method based on ultrafast detection which may include spatial filtering that allows us to study the dynamics and structure of the individual RL spikes. A model based on an exponential probability distribution of photon path lengths in an amplifying medium is proposed. The spectro-temporal evolution and the energetic behavior of the SSRL emission predicted by the model accord well with the different time windows used in the experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Is the Weak Coupling Nonlinear SDM Channel Worse Than the Strong Coupling One?
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The two working regimes of strong (SCR) and weak coupling (WCR) for multimode fibers (MMF) for space-division multiplexing are compared in terms of nonlinearity and achievable data rates. Leveraging recently developed perturbative models and considerations on MMF parameters, hints are provided that the WCR can achieve similar or higher rates than the SCR. Some considerations on power allocation over frequency channels and modes are provided.

articleTitle: Large Rabi splitting and Purcell factor in coupled Ag metamaterial cavity and MoS2 monolayer
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Strong coupling (SC) between plasmons and excitons gives rise to a plasmon-exciton hybridized state. These hybrid states exhibit large Rabi splitting with spectral anti-crossing behavior and ultrafast energy exchange compared to the decay rates of the plasmonic and exciton modes. Therefore, to create efficient nanoscale devices based on the principle of SC, it is essential to combine high-quality cavities with stable, high-oscillator-strength quantum emitters. Herein, we propose a silver plasmonic metamaterial cavity (Ag cavity) with a monolayer of molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) to investigate SC phenomena at room temperature, which are promising for constructing compact and high-performance quantum optical devices. The strong light confinement by the Ag cavity induces scalable Rabi splitting and an ultrahigh Purcell factor (Fp). Consequently, SC and spontaneous emission enhancement of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the hybrid structures have been numerically studied. It is found that an ultrahigh $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{p}}\left(\gt8 \times 10^{4}\right)$ and a Rabi splitting of greater than 117 meV can be easily achieved by varying the cavity gaps and the thickness of the Ag nanostructures. This design has enormous potential in manipulating the spontaneous emission of the emitter, which is crucial for development of low-threshold polariton laser, high-purity single-photon emitters, and quantum computing.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional Layered Material-Based Nonlinear Optical Upconverters
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Two-dimensional layered materials are emerging as promising nonlinear optical media due to their order crystalline arrangement, strong nonlinear optical susceptibility, interesting layer dependence of optical properties, high refractive index, broad transparency window, and ease of fabricating devices using dry-transfer and nanoscale patterning techniques. In this work, an overview of some of our efforts to realize frequency upconversion devices using multilayer two-dimensional layered material in Fabry Perot cavity [1, 2] and sub-wavelength disk structures [3] will be presented. Up-conversion is particularly an important functionality to convert optical signals from wavelengths were good quality detectors are not available to the visible or near infrared range, where good quality silicon based detectors are widely used. Such up-conversion functionalities find key applications in infrared spectroscopy and imaging. Traditionally, bulky nonlinear optical crystals requiring careful phase-matching have been used for up-conversion. Recently, there is interest performing upconversion using miniaturized structures such as sub-wavelength metasurfaces and two-dimensional layered materials. First, inverse design of such structures using hybrid genetic optimization and particle swarm optimization in order to determine the structure dimensions with the goal of maximizing the far-field radiated nonlinear optical signal will be discussed. The fabrication of these structures using standard cleanroom processing techniques and the experimental characterization of the fabricated structures using linear reflectance and nonlinear optical studies will be discussed. The future outlook of such materials being utilized for mainstream nonlinear photonic applications will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Toward Increasing Switching Capacity of Twisted and Folded Clos Network Guaranteeing Admissible Blocking Probability
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Anticipated is the establishing of a future data center network, built with a Clos network comprising optical-circuit switches to manage the increasing traffic volume. A twisted and folded Clos network (TF-Clos) expands the switching capacity under a strict non-blocking (SNB) condition compared to a folded Clos network. If we relax the SNB condition, where we allow an admissible blocking probability, it is feasible to increase the switching capacity more. This paper proposes a refined version of our developed design model, guaranteeing an admissible blocking probability. We show the effectiveness of the refined model regarding the switching capacity and computation time.

articleTitle: A Simplified FSO Channel Model with Weak Turbulence and Pointing Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Free-space optical (FSO) links suffer from atmospheric turbulence and pointing errors. The probability density function (PDF) describing the distribution of the fading coefficient that models such effects is of great importance for designing FSO systems. In this paper, we present a simple closed-form approximation for this PDF in the weak turbulence regime. Our proposed approximation involves only exponential functions. This approximation is then used to develop two simple bit error rate expressions for on-off keying. Numerical results show excellent accuracy of the proposed expressions.

articleTitle: Pragmatic Authentication Technique in Fiber Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The Passive Optical Network (PON) is recognized as a crucial facilitator of broadband optical access networks globally. The enhanced bandwidth demand has led to generational upgrades in PON technology. These upgrades should also encompass technologies for security enhancements at all network levels. In this paper, we propose a novel authentication technique for enhancing physical layer security in fiber optical networks. This technique enables authentication for the user end, network subsystems, and the optical path, by utilizing their intrinsic individual properties. This method relies on using an optical physical unclonable function (OPUF) approach for optical authentication. We have demonstrated this technique’s performance in point-to-point (P2P) and PON systems for both the user end and Fiber to the X (FTTX) authentication. We compared our proposed authentication technique with existing methods, evaluating their advantages and disadvantages in terms of cost, complexity, and implementation. We assessed the resilience of our proposed technique against critical physical and digital attacks through different metrics.

articleTitle: Rainbow light trapping in a chirped 3D woodpile photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The so called “rainbow trapping” effect (wavelength dependent light localization) is demonstrated in a chirped 3D woodpile photonic crystal in the visible and near infrared regimes. By varying the period in the propagation direction, the 3D structure is designed to progressively slow down the incident wave and to localize different wavelengths at different positions. A first experiment in the visible range shows good qualitative results, with green localizing near the beginning of the crystal and red propagating deeper. The measurements in the infrared regime show strong localization between 1400nm and 1700nm. This localization goes deeper into the crystal as the wavelength increases, agreeing nicely with our numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Temperature measurement utilizing tilted Bragg gratings in solution-filled specialty optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this work, we propose a tilted fiber Bragg grating (TFBG) sensor for temperature measurements. The grating is inscribed using a femtosecond laser and the line-by-line (LbL) direct writing technique in the central core of a specialty optical fiber. The channel filled with glycerol aqueous solution beside the central core significantly improves the temperature sensitivity of the TFBG cladding modes due to its high thermo-optic coefficient (TOC). We show that the temperature sensitivity of the core mode is $9.59 \mathrm{pm} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, while the counterparts of the cladding modes reach up to $-29.45 \mathrm{pm} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in the range of $20-40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

articleTitle: Natural gas composition analysis with Quartz Tuning Fork-based spectroscopic techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Petrochemical industry operations can be optimized detecting hydrocarbons in the gas phase. Laser-based spectroscopic sensors are well suited for this application since they proved to be highly selective and sensitive. We report on two different optical techniques for natural gas composition assessment, both implementing quartz tuning forks as sensitive elements: quartz enhanced photoacoustic spectroscopy and light-induced thermo-elastic spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Tailoring light spectrum in silicon photonics chips with high-performance optical filter
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Integrated photonics filters are essential components in current optical systems, spanning from telecommunications to quantum information processing or biosensing. One method for implementing optical filters in silicon photonics platforms involves periodically modulating the refractive index along the direction of propagation. This modulation directly influences the spectral characteristics of the structure, facilitating the implementation of arbitrary spectral responses through careful design of the index modulation profile. In this presentation, we summarize our recent progress in leveraging such filters to demonstrate multiband spectral responses, polarization-independent filters, high-rejection filters, and sideband-tunable notch spectral responses.

articleTitle: Vector Subharmonic Entrainment
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We report on theoretical and experimental study of a new vector type of the subharmonic entrainment (SHE) in a fiber laser mode locked by Nonlinear Polarization Rotation (NPR). We demonstrated that SHE between the NPR-driven lasing oscillations and injected continuous wave (CW) signal with evolving state of polarization can support stable soliton breathing dynamics.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Extension Using Raman Amplifier for Enhanced Optical Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper presents an exploration of bandwidth extension in optical communication systems towards L band through the integration of Raman amplifiers. By employing a Raman amplifier, the usable bandwidth of the optical fiber can be significantly extended, enhancing the capacity and performance of modern high-speed networks. We investigate the theoretical foundations and practical implementations of Raman amplifiers in L-band, detailing gain characteristics and noise performance. Our findings suggest that Raman amplifiers are a viable solution for addressing the increasing demand for higher data rates and expanded bandwidth in optical communication systems.

articleTitle: CVD-prepared PbSe films for mid-IR photodetectors with high detectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In order to obtain the layers of lead selenide, in this work we used the Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) method, implemented on a setup for the synthesis of chalcogenide structures, which we described in detail in [1–5]. Elementary high-purity lead (5N) and selenium (5N) were used as the starting materials, and high-purity argon was used as a carrier gas. Sensibilization of the resulting films was carried out in two stages: annealing in air and then iodination. The influence of annealing conditions in air and iodination on the surface morphology and photoelectric properties of the final films was studied.

articleTitle: Photonic Integrated Circuit Assisted Photothermal Spectroscopy of liquids and Gases
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We will describe our recent work on on-chip photothermal spectroscopy of samples in both gaseous and liquid phases and will show how this technique can be used to realize compact highly sensitive and selective sensors for a range of analytes.

articleTitle: Hollow Core Inhibited Coupling Fibers: theoretical and real limits
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this work we present theoretical and numerical tools and apply them for analyzing the main performance limits of Hollow Core Inhibited Coupling Fibers, highlighting the ultimate limits in ideal fibers and the current limits coming from non-idealities of real fibers.

articleTitle: Enhancement of RE ions emission by silica glass nanostructuring
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Silicate-based glass represents an established material for the fabrication of lasers and amplifiers thanks to excellent material properties, such as thermal stability, mechanical and chemical resistance, as well as low cost and feasible mass-scale fabrication. However, the silica network represents an unsuitable environment for RE ions. The RE ions act as network modifiers, which primarily form ionic bonds with non-bonding oxides in the silica network. In pure silica glass, the RE ions tend to form clusters, which leads to concentration quenching. Additionally, the high phonon energy of silica lattice is responsible for high rates of multiphonon relaxation. To remediate these drawbacks, various strategies were proposed and explored in the past decades. One of these strategies is the modification of the glass network, i.e., nanostructuring of the glass matrix by metal nanoparticles or by oxidic nanoparticles, where the RE is part of a single crystalline nanoparticle and the associated technological conditions in the preparation of the optical fiber. This contribution presents an overview of recent advances in preparation of various metallic or oxidic nanoparticles in silicate glass matrix and the effect on RE ion emission.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a graphene-based metasurface modulator for 6G wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing development of 6 G wireless communication, Terahertz waves have attracted significant attention. Their unique properties, such as vast bandwidth and minimal interference, make them ideal for high-speed wireless systems. In this context, graphene is considered a key material: its properties make it perfect for implementing the components needed for future 6 G communication In this paper, we propose the design of a transparent graphene-based modulator working in the range between 1 THz and 5 THz. We investigate several configurations using different pairs of graphene chemical potentials, incarnating the two states of a binary encoding. The optimal configuration has been evaluated by means of a figure of merit properly defined. This device paves the way for the realization of a new class of smart components for 6 G wireless communications.

articleTitle: Coupled oscillators’ approach to modelling a graphene-based plasmonic sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Sensing based on surface plasmon resonances (SPRs) is a popular idea for selectively detecting (bio-) molecules. With plasmon resonances due to noble metals, in the form of thin films or nanoparticles, occurring in the visible spectral range, the selectivity is achieved by functionalizing the surface in order to enhance adhesion of the targeted molecular species. An alternative idea is to use SPRs produced by graphene electrons, in the THz-FIR range, where characteristic vibrational modes of many important molecules occur. It has been demonstrated experimentally with graphene nanoribbon superlattices. Due to superposition of a narrow molecular resonance (dipole-active vibration mode) and the broad plasmonic band, Fano-type resonances were found, caused by an interference between a resonant state (molecular vibration) and a broad continuum (SPR band). Originally predicted as a quantum phenomenon, the Fano resonance has a classical analogy that can be exemplified by coupled harmonic oscillators. We demonstrate the capability of this approach for modelling graphene-based plasmonic sensors and discuss its advantages.

articleTitle: Surface-Acoustic Waves Actuated Amplification in a Plasmonic Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this work, we first experimentally show the effect of voltage controlled surface acoustic waves on localized surface Plasmon (LSP), which unveils exceptional properties of plasmon-phonon interaction. The experiment was conducted by depositing Au nanoparticles on an X-cut LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> to generate plasmonic oscillation, and fabricating an interdigital transducer monolithically to create surface acoustic wave pulses. The interaction between amplitude acoustic wave and plasmonic oscillation affects different plasmon dynamics and relaxation gradients, leading to a systematic change in LSP absorption. Based on the experimental results of plasmonic-phonon interactions, we next propose a new method to amplify the propagating plasmons through an external on-chip surface acoustic signal. We increase the plasmonic intensity gain of 1.08 dB by providing an external excitation in the form of SAW at a peak-to-peak potential swing of 3V, utilizing a single chip.

articleTitle: Influence of contra-directional couplers’ design parameters in optical filtering for telecommunications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this paper, a systematic study on some of the main design parameters of contra-directional couplers (CDCs) was performed. CDCs with different gaps and corrugation sizes were designed, simulated, fabricated and experimentally characterized in order to understand the influence of each parameter on their spectral response and performance. The fabricated SOI devices help us understand the impact of fabrication in the performance of the devices and also the influence of each parameter in the most important figures of merit when applied to telecommunications

articleTitle: Complete inelastic transparency of time-modulated resonant photonic circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: A time-modulated microstructure that performs the lossless resonant transformation of a wave with a single frequency $\omega_{1}$ to a wave with another single frequency $\omega_{2}$ (rather than a comb of frequencies) exhibits an effect that can be referred to as complete inelastic resonant transparency (CIRT). This effect, predicted three decades ago [1], has been recently experimentally demonstrated in photonics [2]. A light beam with frequency $\omega_{1}$ entering a circuit of coupled microresonators modulated with frequency $\omega_{p}$ can exit it with frequency $\omega_{2}=\omega_{1} \pm$ $\omega_{p}$ and close to unity amplitude. Advantageously, the authors of Ref. [2] proposed photonic circuits modulated with frequency $\omega_{p}$, which potentially allow the complete inelastic conversion of light from frequency $\omega$ to frequency $\omega_{2}=\omega_{1} \pm(N-1) \omega_{p}$ by cascading light between N eigenstates with equally spaced eigenfrequencies. Here, we introduce and investigate a broad class of time-modulated photonic circuits exhibiting CIRT. As examples, we consider circuits of ring microresonators and SNAP microresonators.

articleTitle: Self-starting all-fibered Erbium-doped Mamyshev oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Mamyshev oscillators are known for their capacity of generating high-quality ultrashort pulses. However, their intricate design and self-starting challenges have limited their practical use. In our work, we have experimentally established the first simple and compact structure of a fully fibered erbium doped Mamyshev oscillator that is started thanks to nonlinear polarization evolution mechanism and the full overlapping of the two tunable filters used in our laser cavity. The obtained regime based on Mamyshev mechanism exhibit noise-like pulse mode-locking (NLP-ML) regime. The simplicity and ease of use of our setup would be ideal for further investigations regarding their different output patterns.

articleTitle: Towards Extending Switching Capabilities in Future Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The substantial increase of global data traffic in recent years, driven primarily by the advent of innovative applications and services, is expected to persist and significantly influence the development and implementation of next-generation optical networks. In particular, new flexible and scalable switching architectures capable to support the increasing demand for higher capacities will be envisioned. On this regard, extending current switching capabilities towards including the exploitation of spectral and spatial degrees of freedom will be a suitable option to meet the expected traffic increase and capacity needs. Specifically, new transmission bands, beyond the C-band, and different spatial channels such as fiber cores/modes or even bundles of fibers will enable to provide the expected capacity scaling enhancing the available network resources. Multiband (MB) and spatial division multiplexing (SDM) technologies arise as key technologies to exploit the full potential of the network in terms of rate/bandwidth, flexibility and efficiency. Hence, an innovative MBoSDM switching prototype is here presented and experimentally validated as a possible key solution to be adopted in future optical networks. The main capabilities/features and programmable elements of the proposed node approach are also analyzed.

articleTitle: Clustering and Classification of Fungal Cells and PMMA Microparticles: Unsupervised and Supervised Learning using K-Means, PCA, Logistic Regression and Spiking Neural Networks on Event-Based Cytometry Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Imaging flow cytometry (IFC) is a powerful analytical technique used for rapidly categorizing small cells and micro-particles. Unlike traditional microscopy, IFC instruments handle a high throughput of cells. Typically, photodetectors, photomultiplier tubes, or high-speed frame-based cameras are employed for this task. This study explores the potential of neuromorphic cameras, also known as event-based sensors (EVS), as a detection mechanism for cytometers. While previous work focused on PMMA microparticles, this investigation centers on fungal cells. Moreover, while earlier research leaned towards supervised learning algorithms like logistic regression and spiking neural networks, our approach in this paper employs k-means, an unsupervised learning paradigm. We demonstrate that training such a simple algorithm in conjunction with PCA achieves 100% classification accuracy without relying on training labels.

articleTitle: Joint Fragmentation- and QoT-Aware RBMSA in Dynamic Multi-Band Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Efficient utilization of fiber bandwidth is essential for reducing the total cost of ownership associated with deploying new fiber plants. One of the challenges in dynamic multi-band elastic optical networks (DMB-EONs) is spectrum fragmentation. It stems from the wavelength continuity constraint, the dynamic arrival and departure of service requests, and variations in quality of transmission (QoT) across the wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) channels. This study introduces a QoT-aware algorithm for routing, band, modulation format and spectrum assignment (RBMSA) that considers the spectrum fragmentation along each channel to reduce service blocking ratio (SBR) in DMB-EONs. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm reduces SBR by up to $33.2 \%$ compared to a reference RBMSA algorithm that considers only QoT at the cost of increasing the average path length by $4.4 \%$.

articleTitle: Er-doped rare earth oxides for optical quantum memory on Si substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Quantum memory is a key device for quantum repeaters that are a prerequisite for building global quantum networks. In particular for on-chip quantum memory operating at the telecommunication wavelength, Er-doped $\mathrm{CeO}_{2}\left(\mathrm{Er}: \mathrm{CeO}_{2}\right)$ is a promising material platform, in which a long coherence time is expected. This is because the Er ions are dilutely embedded in the nuclear-spin-free CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> matrix (crystal). Although we have prepared high-quality Er: CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> crystals on Si substrates by molecular beam epitaxy, further improvement of their optical properties is desired. Here, we introduced a post-growth annealing process and explored the optimum annealing conditions using Bayesian optimization with a view to increasing the intensity and narrowing the optical absorption linewidth. The post-growth annealing process turned out to be effective, and the resultant improvement in the optical properties can be attributed to improved crystallinity of the host material CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> that contributes to providing a uniform environment around the Er ions.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Photonic Accelerators in Neuromorphic Computing via Structure Trimming
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Due to the low latency and parallelism of light, photonic neuromorphic accelerators are expected to realize high-speed computing with low energy consumption, thus meeting the exponentially growing computing demands brought about by the continuous development of artificial intelligence. However, the optical response of many photonic structures used in photonic accelerators depends on their geometry and is thus sensitive to fabrication errors. In this paper, silicon ion implantation, as an emerging post-trimming method, is used to effectively tune the optical response of silicon nitride ring resonators and asymmetric directional couplers. Silicon ion implantation locally alters the material and thus the effective refractive index of the guided mode. Due to the properties of silicon, silicon ion implantation causes negligible loss to the structures at an operating wavelength of 1550 nm, and the trimming is non-volatile. After implantation, ring resonator transmission spectra can be shifted from 6 pm to several nanometres. Further, the transmission change of the asymmetric directional coupler was 17 dB. Silicon ion implantation provides an excellent platform for the non-volatile tuning of photonic structures, facilitating the scaling of photonic neuromorphic accelerators and ultimately advancing artificial intelligence-based applications.

articleTitle: Unpolarized light: Poincaré Sphere Engineering - From natural light via quantum optics to applications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We investigate the polarization properties of unpolarized light, first in the temporal domain realized by $1.55 \mu \mathrm{m}$ ASE light emitted by an erbium-doped fiber amplifier and second in the spatial domain by exploiting the polarization dispersion of a Cornu depolarizer. We find novel Stokes parameter correlations and invariances for temporally unpolarized light and novel states on the Poincaré sphere for spatially unpolarized light. All these results give new fresh insight into the field of classical polarization with interesting promising quantum and sensing application perspectives.

articleTitle: Protection Methods Analysis in a Hybrid C/C+L Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The use of multi-band elastic optical networks (MB-EONs) over $\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{L}$ bands is considered as a realistic mediumterm solution to extend the capacity of current C-band optical networks. In this kind of networks, different levels of survivability can be offered, as we showed in a previous work in which we analysed the impact of these techniques in fully upgraded $\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{L}$ networks. However, postponing the high CAPEX cost of activating the L-band for all the optical fibers within a network has shifted the attention of the network operators to partially upgraded networks. Thus, we now focus on partially upgraded networks and demonstrate that it is necessary to modify the protection method that we previously proposed for fully upgraded networks in order to efficiently work in these environments. The performance of the modified method is then evaluated in terms of request blocking ratio in both partially and fully upgraded networks, and we show that the introduced variation outperforms the original method.

articleTitle: Multicarrier Transmission Optimization in Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This study investigates the trade-off between Quality of Transmission (QoT) performance and spectrum efficiency through low-margin operation of multicarriers. Margin reduction is enabled by implementing tight filtering and slight subcarriers overlap. Experiments conducted on a Software Defined Networking (SDN)-controlled Elastic Optical Network (EON) testbed demonstrate spectrum-efficient multicarriers composed of three subcarriers, achieving savings of up to 22% in spectrum occupation for 80 km optical connections.

articleTitle: In-network Control for Flow Steering
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In recent years monitoring networks with high level of accuracy is becoming crucial to meet performance and security requirements of data flows. Concurrently, automated communication service assurance calls for increased network visibility and faster control loops. To this end, we demonstrate a new proposition that employs in-network control and monitoring of traffic flows using In-band Network Telemetry. Our solution enables rapid network reaction times through decisions taken at the data plane.

articleTitle: Optical chirality in metasurfaces empowered by bound states in a continuum
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Maximizing the chiral optical response of metasurfaces is a hot research area in nanophotonics. In this talk, we show that Bound States in a Continuum (BICs) can provide a robust pathway to achieve a high circular dichroism in the optical properties. We focus on dielectric metasurfaces supporting BICs, which are split into Circularly Polarized States (CPS) upon symmetry reduction of the geometric structure. First, we show how BICs and CPS lead to polarization singularities in the far field, whose winding number - or topological charge follows from the symmetry of the lattice [1–4]. Then, we determine the polarization properties via the Stokes parameters, focusing on the conditions for the occurrence of a nonvanishing circular polarization, using both rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA) and analytic modelling. Finally, we relate the optical response to the calculated Stokes parameters, and show that the circular dichroism can be tuned by the degree of symmetry breaking. The results shed light on the role of polarization singularities and symmetry breaking in tailoring the chiroptical response in the far field.

articleTitle: Autonomous Control Operations for Energy-Efficient Packet Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Recent efforts have focused on integrating packet and optical technologies to meet growing broadband demands while enhancing cost and energy efficiency. Within this framework, strategies are oriented towards adopting coherent DWDM small form factor transceivers (pluggables) with the aim of simplifying IPoWDM networks. This study specifically examines two IPoWDM network scenarios. The first scenario involves the use of traditional external transponders situated between routers and the optical line system. In the second scenario, transponders are eliminated, and routers’ ports are equipped with transceiver pluggables directly connected to ROADMs. The power consumption of the involved network elements for each scenario are detailed. Additionally, we explore the autonomous operations managed by a SDN controller when dynamically provisioning connectivity services targeting the reduction of the network power consumption. To this end, an SDN controller architecture is presented offloading the computationally intensive routing function to an externalized server. The workflow, functions, and APIs used by the SDN controller are detailed. Particularly, it is presented potential extensions to the ONF TAPI Context for describing transceiver power-consumptions attributes required when dynamically executing energy-aware path computations.

articleTitle: Integrating the synchronization stacks of a heterogeneous time-sensitive networking system with wired and wireless domains
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This contribution recounts the experience and main integration challenges of the different precision time protocol (PTP)-based synchronization stacks present in the demonstrator of the heterogeneous time-sensitive networking (TSN) architecture of the TIMING project with wired and wireless segments. This demonstrator represents a significant initiative aimed at showcasing the feasibility of deploying complex, real-time industrial control and robotics systems over large areas by leveraging the deterministic and resilient transport capabilities of TSN in combination with advanced orchestration, optimization methodologies, and commercial telecommunication networks. The end-to-end distribution of a unified time reference is essential to achieve a successful integration. To that end, it is imperative to verify the interoperability between the PTP stacks of the different segments of the network. Hence, we focus on the description of the main scenarios, challenges, and hurdles that had to be overcome to allow the seamless propagation of PTP between the wireless-TSN devices and the Ethernet-based TSN switches present in the demonstrator. This will include an analysis of the applicable profiles and configuration options, suitable for the demonstrator, their effects on performance, as well as lessons learned during the process and considerations for future large-scale deployments of TSN systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Step Traffic Prediction for Multi-Period Planning in Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: A multi-period planning framework is proposed that exploits multi-step ahead traffic predictions to address service overprovisioning and improve adaptability to traffic changes, while ensuring the necessary quality-of-service (QoS) levels. An encoder-decoder deep learning model is initially leveraged for multi-step ahead prediction by analyzing real-traffic traces. This information is then exploited by multi-period planning heuristics to efficiently utilize available network resources while minimizing undesired service disruptions (caused due to lightpath re-allocations), with these heuristics outperforming a single-step ahead prediction approach.

articleTitle: Offloading computing from your headsets - how viable is a HomeCloud?
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Demand for computing in households is increasing fast, due to the increased demand for Virtual, Augmented, or Mixed Reality to achieve an immersive user experience. Expensive and energy-hungry headsets and smart devices with increased computing and communication capacity are being built. Yet, as users spend more time on such devices, the computing power of personal desktop or laptop devices are often left unused. An interesting question to ask is: can we use available personal computing power to make headset lighter, cheaper and more durable? In this study, we investigate the concept of a HomeCloud, where computations on portable smart devices can be offloaded to household personal computers. We investigate how the energy efficiency of mobile computing and wireless transmission technologies, and the storage density of portable device batteries, may affect the gain one can achieve in a HomeCloud. We also study the impact of computing resource availability and smart device use pattern on battery life.

articleTitle: Enhanced-backscattering optical fibers for inline interferometers: applications to biosensing
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The interrogation of Rayleigh backscattering in single-mode optical fibers is a key asset for the development of distributed fiber-optic sensors operating in frequency- and time-domain. In order to increase the return signal, fibers with high backscattering have been introduced, exploiting weak random gratings or UV exposure; however the most viable method relies on introducing high doses or nanoparticles directly into the fiber core, which allows reaching scattering increments consistently over 50 dB. In this work, we discuss the use of such fibers for interferometry; exploiting its high backscattering, a short span of enhanced backscattering fiber can act as a random cavity, achieving a semi-stochastic spectrum that can be interrogated with a spectral analyzer. We present some of the recent applications in biosensing, including the detection of poxvirus proteins in wastewater and the detection of retinal biomarkers in tears.

articleTitle: Harmful attacks threat and counteracting them in optical networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Optical communication is considered as safe. However, the situation looks different when attackers gain physical access to infrastructure (optical fibre cables or devices installed in the network nodes), with the purpose of eavesdropping or deterioration of such transmission (harmful attacks). Therefore, the awareness of such vulnerabilities get key meaning of design so-called intelligent networks of a new generation, which are able to protect themselves against such attacks in real time, automatically, using of ML algorithms for this purpose among others. The paper summarises different types of such attacks, togethers with outline of methods their realisation, distinguishing them on passive (eavesdropping) and active (disrupting, jamming). Protection methods based on the machine learning approach were also rediscussed at the end.

articleTitle: Disorder-Enhanced Photonic Crystals based on-chip Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Existing high-resolution spectrometers are cumbersome and costly. we aim to create an affordable, on-chip spectrometer by developing an efficient wavelength separation system using disorder-enhanced photonic crystal lattices. © 2022 The Author(s)

articleTitle: Blocking Probability Analysis Modeling in Spectrally-Spatially Elastic Optical Networks: A Crosstalk-Avoided Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Crosstalk presents a well-defined challenging issue in spectrally-spatially elastic optical networks (SS-EONs), leading to increased blocking probability (BP). Analyzing BP analytically becomes complex due to additional constraints. Current assessments of BP in SS-EONs, particularly in multi-core multi-mode fiber (MCMMF)-based systems, heavily rely on simulation-based techniques. This paper analyzes an accurate analytical model based on a continuous-time Markov chain in SS-EONs, investigating various spectrum allocation policies with and without the spectrum contiguity constraint. To calculate BP, the analytical model produces all feasible states and their transitions while mitigating inter-core and inter-mode crosstalks. Numerical results show that analytical model and simulation studies have lower BP with CMS-FF and CMS-RF using without contiguity constraints compared to other schemes.

articleTitle: Access-Point to Access-Point Connectivity for PON-based OWC Spine and Leaf Data Centre Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
