The real-time distributed mapping of slow-varying low-amplitude processes (previously inaccessible to traditional DAS), could provide unique advantages and high impact measurements, ranging from earthquake wave propagation, to the measurement of infragravity waves, earth and ocean tides, and, ultimately, being compatible with the mapping of day-to-year-long tectonic plaque movements.

articleTitle: Fiber based photonic sensor for sensing of vital bio-signs and of glucose concentration in blood stream as well as for its usage in smart building related applications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this presentation, we introduce a new technique for fiber based noninvasive sensing. The sensor consists of a laser, a multi-mode optical fiber, video camera and a computer. The operation principle is based on tracking of temporal variations in the speckle patterns field generated by interference of the light modes within the fiber when it is subjected to deformation. The speckle patterns are created when the light at the tip of the fiber is diffracted through a diffuser and imaged by a camera. The fiber-based sensor is used for bio-medical applications such as monitoring of vital bio-signs as respiration, heart beats and blood pressure even when integrating it into a fabric to provide non-tight contact wearable wellness monitoring device. It can also be used as a non-wearable portable sensor to estimate, in a non-invasive way, the concentration of glucose in the blood stream when the measurement is combined with external magnetic excitation to use Faraday rotation property of glucose for its sensing. It can also be applied for non-biomedically related applications such as detection of water leakages along water pipes while in this case the fiber-based sensor is integrated along the water pipes. In all cases and applications, machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms are applied on the video of the time changing speckle patterns that is captured by the imaging camera. The algorithms extract from those changes the specific parameter that the fiber sensor is designated to sense. In allof the above-mentioned three types of applications, we will show experimental validation for the proposed sensing schemes.

articleTitle: Flexible Blind Information Reconciliation for QKD based on Rateless Protograph LDPC codes
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Information Reconciliation (IR) is a crucial step in the process of distillation of unconditionally secure keys in Quantum key distribution (QKD). Novel IR rateless codes based on protograph low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes have been recently designed to replace Cascade. In this paper, a blind IR protocol is described that exploits all the features of rateless protograph LDPC codes.

articleTitle: Edge Orchestration Framework for AI-assisted Link Failure Forecasting and Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: A comprehensive orchestration framework designed for edge computing scenarios is presented. The framework includes (i) a telemetry collector gathering data from both computing and programmable packet-optical network elements; (ii) a Service Level Agreement (SLA) broker processing telemetry data and enforcing configurations at the network, computing and/or application level; (iii) a lightweight Software Defined Networking (SDN) controller designed for low-latency operations over wired-wireless networks including Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs); (iv) a Kubernetes scheduler for pod relocation; and (v) an Application API module to trigger adaptations at the application level. In this paper, first implementations of an AI-empowered SLA Broker and of a lightweight SDN Controller are presented, showing the capability to dynamically forecast critical link degradations and successfully recover adequate network conditions without affecting the service level.

articleTitle: Low-temperature perovskites thin films solar cell
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Hybrid organic-inorganic halide perovskites have become the most promising materials in photovoltaics. In just a few years, the energy conversion efficiency of hybrid perovskite solar cells has increased dramatically from an initial bright value of 9% to over 24%. Their remarkable properties, including high carrier mobility, low carrier recombination rate, and tunable spectral absorption range, are attributed to the unique electronic properties of these materials. Despite the undoubted progress in the conversion efficiency of perovskite solar cells, understanding hybrid perovskites’ basic structural, optical, and electrical properties is limited. The presentation will include the research results on the relationship between low-temperature structural, electrical, and optical properties of multifunctional hybrid perovskite thin films produced by the unique physical vapor co-deposition (PVco-D) technique. The experimental study will be compared with theoretical simulations performed using SCAPS 1D software.

articleTitle: On the Trade-off between the Maximum Capacity and the Length of a Multicore Fiber Link
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The transmission capacity of a multicore fiber (MCF) link is the sum of the capacities of its cores, but the capacity of each core depends not only on the modulation format (MF) and baud rate (BR) of the lightpaths established through the core but also on the inter-core crosstalk (XT) impairments imposed by the adjacent cores in use. For a MCF link of a given length, we propose a Binary Linear Programming formulation to determine the MF and the BR to use on each core, aiming to reach the MCF maximum capacity. Comparing the maximum capacity of a 19-core MCF with the single core fiber counterpart, the influence of the link length on the MCF capacity scaling factor reached by MCFs is characterized.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Enabled Directly Modulated Lasers
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The complex dynamics of systems based on directly modulated lasers (DMLs) can hinder their optimization, as their simulation entails numerical methods where gradient calculation is not readily available. Our proposed solution combines data-driven DML modeling with end-to-end (E2E) learning techniques to obtain optimal link configurations.

articleTitle: Field Trial of an ML-Assisted Phase-Sensitive OTDR for Traffic Monitoring in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We present a field trial of cost-effective distributed optical fiber sensing (DOFS) for traffic intensity estimation. The field trial uses a buried single-mode fiber installed along the university campus intended for communications and research experimentation. Acquired $\phi$-OTDR traces are concatenated and transformed into a space-time domain to form images. The resulting images are then processed by a MobileNetv2 model for car counting. Training is carried out by a set of collected images labeled by traffic information gathered automatically from camera videos processed with the novel YOLOv8 model. The results indicate that the implemented setup successfully counts heavy vehicles with high accuracy. The setup is also applied to data sets collected over entire days, showcasing its successful application for traffic monitoring in smart cities.

articleTitle: Transparent antenna with reconfigurable pattern based on programmable graphene parasitic elements
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel transparent antenna designed with reconfigurable graphene elements in the sub-THz frequencies. The antenna, with a circular polyimide substrate, leverages a pair of symmetrical fan-blade-shaped parasitic elements and a radiating dipole, each made of graphene. Through programming the operating state of each parasitic element by modifying the graphene chemical potential (2 discrete values are used, 0 eV for the OFF state and 1 eV for the ON state), the antenna’s current distribution is altered, resulting in four distinct configurations of the radiation pattern in the azimuthal plane. The investigation reveals that the lowest S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> value of -37.4 dB is obtained at 200 GHz, with a -10 dB bandwidth that extends from 187 GHz to 214 GHz. The corresponding maximum realized gain is about 2.78 dBi.

articleTitle: Gas-filled Hollow-core Fiber Lasers and Advanced Optoelectronic Neural Interfaces for the Brain (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This work presents our recent research on the development of high pulse energy and narrow linewidth fiber lasers spanning from the near-infrared to the mid-infrared spectral domains, based on different antiresonant hollow-core fibers filled with active gases. We then discuss how the obtained lasers are used for photoacoustic gas sensing and bioimaging, such as real-time detection of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with sub-ppm concentration and brain imaging. In the second part of this invited paper, we briefly present the development of novel multi-functional optoelectronic fibers with integrated metallic electrodes and microfluidic channels for electrophysiology and drug delivery in the brain, respectively with chronic and acute in vivo results.

articleTitle: Hollow core fibres: the long and winding road from scientific tool to commercial product
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Hollow core fibres have been conceived theoretically over a century ago and first demonstrated at the beginning of this millennium. For a couple of decades, their main impact has been mostly in the support of scientific experiments in academic labs around the world. In the last few years, thanks to substantial improvements in optical performance, they are beginning to carve themselves commercial opportunities in various markets, including that of optical communications. In this talk we will review the past challenges and hint at some of the future forthcoming opportunities.

articleTitle: Optical fiber integrated functional elements fabricated by two-photon polymerization
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Optical fibers are one of the most extensively used and powerful devices in the fields of medicine, sensing, power delivery and communication due to their ultra-compact size and low optical loss. Over the last years, researchers have been trying to further enhance the capabilities of this technology by integrating functional structures onto the fibers. This has enabled various applications in micro-optics, such as sensing, imaging and optical trapping. However, the non-planar surface of the optical fibers as well as the small and delicate area of their tip makes the use of standard micro- and nanofabrication techniques extremely challenging. On the contrary, two-photon polymerization (2PP), owing to its high versatility, holds great promise for fabricating advanced functional elements on fibers. Here, we review recent progress on optical fiber integrated functional devices enabled by 2PP.

articleTitle: Ultrafast photodetectors at Terahertz frequencies based on 2D materials: technological developments and applications in optical communications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Bi-dimensional nano-materials and related heterostructures are establishing themselves as intriguing material systems for the development of electronic, photonic and plasmonic quantum devices with properties that can be engineered "from scratch". Their peculiar band-structure and electron transport characteristics, which can be easily manipulated via layer thickness control, indeed suggest they could also form the basis for a new generation of high-performance devices operating in the Terahertz frequency range ($1-10 \mathrm{THz}$) of the electromagnetic spectrum. This talk will review our latest achievements in the developments of high speed photodetectors at THz frequencies ($2-5 \mathrm{THz}$), and will discuss concrete perspectives for applications in optical communications.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Classical and Hybrid Solutions for Lightpath Security Using Quantum Keys
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Optical communications have enabled high-speed data transmission over long distances. However, data are transmitted plain unless are encrypted on higher layers, e.g., IP and TCP, precisely because of: i) the high data rates; and ii) the need of secure key exchange between the end-points of the optical connection. Meanwhile, quantum enabled cryptography has emerged as a promising solution for securing communications by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics which provides unlimited and unconditional security. Although Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols can deliver quantum keys to distant end-points, there are scenarios where one of them is not within the security perimeter of the quantum network. This demonstration focuses on the intersection of optical communication and quantum security, highlighting the synergies between these two domains and their potential to ensure secure communication networks. We explore the integration of optical communication with quantum technologies and showcase how optical encryption using quantum keys retrieved from QKD and Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) systems is performed. Retrieved keys are expanded to the required rate and then used to encrypt the input data at line speed.

articleTitle: Design of a praseodymium-doped fluoroindate fiber amplifier for medium infrared wavelength range applications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel fiber amplifier based on a praseodymium-doped fluoroindate glass has been designed. The amplification wavelength band is centred around $\lambda_{s}=4 \mu \mathrm{m}$, the pump wavelength is $\lambda_{p}=1550 \mathrm{~nm}$. A homemade computer code has been developed to simulate the amplifier behaviour, taking into account spectroscopical parameters from literature. The electromagnetic investigation of the fiber is developed via a Finite Element Method (FEM) software. Several simulations are performed considering different values of the fiber length and the input pump power, with the aim of obtaining wide wavelength bandwidth.

articleTitle: Advances in Mid-Infrared Low-Loss Hollow-Core Anti-Resonant Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In a step forward in hollow-core fiber technology, our research has yielded two anti-resonant fibers that demonstrate record-low optical losses in the mid-infrared wavelength range. The first has a loss of $0.05 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{m}$ between 3.4-3.6 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ and $0.24 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{m}$ between $4.5-4.6 \mu \mathrm{m}$, setting a new benchmark for low loss in this spectral region. The second fiber has a transmission window at longer wavelength, 4.1-6 $\mu \mathrm{m}$, also with a notably low loss, measured as $\sim 7 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{m}$ at $6 \mu \mathrm{m}$, but potentially with lower fundamental mode loss. These fibers are also capable of transmitting laser light, with the first efficiently transmitting the near-diffraction-limited light generated by a tunable optical parametric oscillator and delivering a peak power of 1.1 kW through 108 meters, with a coupling efficiency of $\sim 70 \%$. The second fiber facilitated the delivery of light from a quantum cascade laser, achieving a maximum delivered power of 3.4 mW at $6.045 \mu \mathrm{m}$ over a 0.9 -meter length. These advances represent a substantial improvement in reducing transmission loss, enhancing the overall efficiency and usability of MIR fiber systems, and demonstrates their potential for practical applications. (©2024 The Author(s)

articleTitle: Photophysical study of 2,3-Diphenyl Quinoxaline thin films for potential applications in optoelectronic devices
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: 2,3-Diphenyl Quinoxaline (DPQ) was deposited as a thin film using physical vapor deposition (PVD) on glass and silicon substrates, and its physical properties were thoroughly examined using various techniques. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis revealed a highly rough surface morphology. Optical properties were assessed through transmittance and absorbance measurements, aiding in determining the band gap energy at 3.34 eV. Photoluminescence (PL) and thermal photoluminescence spectroscopy highlighted the material’s strong emission, with decay time confirming its fluorescence nature. Current-voltage characteristics were studied through implementation in a p-n junction, showcasing DPQ’s suitability as both an electron and hole transporting layer in optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Optical Network Emulation (ONE) Engine with Multi-Container Scalability and B400G Signal Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The Optical Network Emulator (ONE) engine is a multi-container software-only solution, designed by the OpNeAR lab at UT Dallas to perform various functionalities of a wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) network in real-time. This paper presents the first real-time demonstration of the ONE engine, customized to emulate a replica of the collaborative demonstration by the OpenROADM and IOWN groups at OFC’24. Leveraging modeling techniques based on polynomial fitting, the software accurately replicates the behavior of transponders, Reconfigurable Add Drop Multiplexing (ROADM) devices, and optical amplifiers. Additionally, the paper explores the scalability of the ONE engine, demonstrating its potential to support larger and more complex network configurations using a single server.

articleTitle: An IPoDWDM Implementation Leveraging OpenROADM Standards for Enhanced Service Orchestration
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper introduces an IP over Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (IPoDWDM) framework that integrates commercial state-of-the-art routing devices and Reconfigurable Optical Add-Drop Multiplexers (ROADMs), adhering to the OpenROADM MSA standards. A hierarchical software-defined networking controller (H-SDNC) seamlessly orchestrates network resource reservation across the DWDM aggregation layer and layer 2/3 through RESTCONF and NETCONF protocols. This first proof of concept paves the way for network architectures that closely integrate multi-layer resources to boost efficiency and flexibility in open and multi-vendor networks.

articleTitle: Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Optical Phased Arrays for reconfigurable on-chip communications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Lithium-niobate-on-insulator (LNOI) technology is an emergent platform for the realization of high-speed and low-loss integrated photonic devices. In this paper, we propose optical wireless switches based on LNOI technology for on-chip communication. In particular, we investigate $1 \times 5$ wireless switch, which exploits optical phased arrays (OPAs) made up of 5 identical taper antennas, and can be used to address 5 in-plane receivers. We first present the design criteria of the Lithium Niobate (LN) taper antenna comprising the OPAs, used both at the transmitter and at the receivers. The implementation of the on-chip wireless switch is then demonstrated by taking into account the multipath propagation effects. We also examine the impact of various geometrical parameters and of the fabrication imperfections on the device performance in terms of insertion loss and crosstalk. We show that the LNOI technology, owing to the remarkable characteristics of LN, could be a good candidate for implementing the on-chip optical wireless switches.

articleTitle: Reflection-mode electro-optical plasmonic modulator: electromagnetic modelling by the method of single expression
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The performed numerical analysis demonstrates an application of a surface plasmon phenomenon for efficient modulation of light intensity in the reflection mode. A supply of modulating high frequency electrical signal to an electro-optical thin layer located upon a thin metallic layer supporting surface plasmons is assumed. The narrow plasmonic and waveguide dips in the angular reflection spectrum are sensitive to the change of the permittivity of the cover electro-optical nano-layer. Numerical analysis is performed for the relevant metal-dielectric multi-nano-layer structure at the oblique incidence of transverse magnetic (TM) wave. For electromagnetic analysis the frequency-domain method of single expression (MSE) is used. The performed analysis permitted to obtain all necessary parameters relevant to the thicknesses of metallic and electro-optic material for efficient optical wave intensity modulation.

articleTitle: Near-infrared and upconversion emission of Tm3+ and Tm3+-Yb3+ codoped transparent oxyfluoride glass-ceramics
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In the present study, oxyfluoride glass-ceramics (GCs) with crystalline phase NaLaF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> doped with TmF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and codoped with YbF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> have been prepared by Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS), and their optical properties characterized and compared with GCs prepared by the conventional thermal treatment method. The spectroscopic properties of the near infrared and upconverted emissions of $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}$ ions have been characterized by using steady-state laser spectroscopy. The energy transfer between $\mathrm{Yb}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}$ ions is confirmed by the near-infrared (NIR) and upconversion emissions after $\mathrm{Yb}^{3+}$ excitation at 975 nm. Back transfer from $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}$ to $\mathrm{Yb}^{3+}$ is also present under near-infrared excitation of $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}$ ions at 791 nm. Blue, red, and NIR upconverted emissions are only observed in $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}-\mathrm{Yb}^{3+}$ codoped samples after 975 nm excitation, thus confirming the effective energy transfer between $\mathrm{Yb}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Tm}^{3+}$ ions.

articleTitle: Ring-Cascaded Sequential Micro-Ring Resonators Array as a Photonic Reservoir for Signal Equalization in Intra-Data Center Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: A novel photonic reservoir using multi-ring resonators is described to perform signal equalization in a short-reach PAM-4 transmission system running at 112 GBaud. The proposed structure enables resonator-based optical feedback, which improves BER compared to DSP-based feed-forward equalization, while requiring only a single photodiode with no additional bandwidth, thereby reducing DSP complexity.

articleTitle: Proactive Relocation for Survivable Cloud Services
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Improving the survivability of optical cloud services is costly due to the numerous resources involved. In this work, we introduce a proactive backup storage relocation (PBSR) strategy, which relocates backup storage in advance to better prepare services for potential failures and reduce the need for reactive relocation. Results show that our proposal enhances availability and restorability without increasing the service blocking ratio, while reactive relocations are reduced by a factor of up to half.

articleTitle: Second-order Nonlinear Disordered Photonics: from versatile wavelength conversion to deep computing
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper explores second-order nonlinear disordered photonic media assembled from oxide nanoparticles, particularly barium titanate and lithium niobate nanocrystals. Thanks to the simultaneous linear scattering and second-harmonic generation, these media favors the emergence of a variety of unexplored optical processes with applications in optical frequency conversion and photonic neuromorphic computing.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Optical Beam Forming Network for Telecom Payloads
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In space communication as well as space-to-ground communication an efficient beam forming network (BFN) feeding the phased arrayed antenna system in satellite telecom payloads plays a pivotal role. Owing to various advantages the microwave photonics based optical BFNs (OBFNs) are found to be more promising to meet the future demand over the traditional electronic BFNs. In this article, a novel OBFN is reported with cascaded coupled-resonator optical waveguides (CROWs) which can simultaneously control the signal bandwidth and group delay. Unlike traditional metallic heater low loss phase change material (PCM) is used to realize the reconfigurability ensuring compact structure and low power consumption. Thanks to localized tunning enabled by PCM and strategic structural implementation, for a fixed bandwidth of 5 GHz the delay can be continuously tuned over 100 ps whereas the bandwidth can be tunned from 4.3 GHz to 7 GHz for a fixed delay, showing a promise towards breaking the constraint present in delay-bandwidth product and find application in 5G-6G wireless communication.

articleTitle: CRIGFs: Spectral filters, but also modal filters and combiners
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: CRIGF filters have been shown to exhibit Fano resonances based on mesoscopic localized modes. We will show how we can harness this to design high Q factor CRIGFs, or use selective excitations of part of these modes to use the CRIGF as modal spatial filters on combiners.

Author Keywords: Fano resonances, spectral filters, modal filters

articleTitle: Quality of Transmission-Aware Optimization of Passive WDM Optical Xhaul Access Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Passive wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) optical technologies are a cost-effective transmission solution for ensuring connectivity in Xhaul networks, transporting radio traffic between remote access nodes and a central site (hub) in 5G radio access networks. The optimization of passive WDM optical Xhaul networks requires careful decisions on routing transmission paths and placing optical add-drop multiplexers (OADMs) to aggregate traffic while maintaining the transmission quality (QoT) to ensure expected transmission reach. This work presents a QoT-aware heuristic algorithm for optimized planning of such networks. The numerical analysis shows the algorithm’s effectiveness in planning the transmission paths aggregating traffic from remote sites using OADMs, particularly considerable cost savings compared to the network without traffic aggregation.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of an Efficient DRL-based Routing and Spectrum Assignment for Optical Network Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This work explores the application of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) for Routing and Spectrum Assignment (RSA) in Elastic Optical Networks (EONs). By capitalizing on the inherent capabilities of DRL to manage complex and dynamic service demands and network conditions, this demo showcases the seamless integration of a DRL approach with an enhanced Software-Defined Networking (SDN) control plane for enabling more intelligent, flexible, and efficient optical network management. We validate this integration by utilizing CTTC’s ADRENALINE testbed®, where a trained DRL agent assisting on the path and resource selection function is effectively interfaced with a full-fledge SDN control plane implementation. This validation confirms both the practical applicability of the DRL approach on supporting selected control functions, and industry-standard interfaces in operational EON infrastructures, while also highlighting the potential for future innovations in optical network automation.

articleTitle: Realizing an indoor OWC system by means of a Luminescent Solar Concentrator
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Optical Wireless Communications (OWC) have the potential to provide new solutions for the communication systems in both indoor and outdoor scenarios. Here, we present an innovative approach for OWC data transmission in indoor environments. We experimentally combined commercial off-the-shelf components i.e., light emitting diodes and photodiodes, with a luminescent solar concentrator. These concentrators are novel for OWC applications; thus, we perform a complete characterization of these devices and of the whole system. To validate this system, a high-definition video optical transmission demonstration is reported.

articleTitle: Flexible and Cost-Efficient Auto-Alignment for Bidirectional Optical Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Optical wireless communication offers a promising solution for flexible high-capacity data transmission due to its immunity to electromagnetic interference. However, unlike fiber optic cables, achieving optimal performance in optical wireless links critically depends on precise alignment between the transmitter and receiver. This study introduces two prototype optical heads, composed of a visible beacon, standard Raspberry Pi camera, and computer vision algorithms to enable bidirectional receiver discovery and fine beam alignment. Using such low-cost, off-the-shelf equipment, we demonstrate that fully successful and reliable alignment can be achieved starting from any blind position within an area of 5 square meters for a link distance of 20 meters.

articleTitle: Cloud Resource Allocation Recommendation Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Resource allocation is a key topic in distributed cloud systems, especially as more and more cloud products and service offerings introduce decision complexity. It’s a common challenge for cloud users to predict usage and budget accordingly. This paper studies the industry practices on smart resource allocation in the cloud and proposes a novel approach using data-driven combination of LSTM and K-means for cloud resource allocation.

articleTitle: Hollow-core fibers with reduced surface roughness for record losses and beam delivery in the UV domain
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We report a new generation of HCPCFs demonstrating ultralow loss in the short-wavelength domain by the use of new fabrication process. The process consists of applying a shear stress on the fiber silica core-surround surface. This approach allows a significant silica surface roughness reduction demonstrated by using a home-made picometer-resolution and high dynamic range profilometer. The surface quality improvement is further corroborated by record optical performances measured in the UV spectral range with losses between $50-10 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{km}$ in the wavelength range of $280-400 \mathrm{~nm}$. As a demonstration of the interest of such fibers, UV laser beam delivery at specific industrial wavelengths including 257/266 nm and $343 / 355 \mathrm{~nm}$ are presented.

articleTitle: Design of a hybrid optical component for the early detection of plant diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The project to which this work relates aims to propose an integrated infrared optical solution to meet the current objective of reducing the use of phytosanitary inputs in agriculture. Its main objective is to prove the feasibility of hybrid optical micro-sensors that will allow early detection of plant diseases, via the detection of spores of phytopathogenic fungi. The innovation produced should make it possible to avoid systematic preventive treatments, thanks to a better targeted decision support. Due to their transparency in the infrared range where many absorption lines of spores are located, chalcogenide glasses are materials of choice for the realization of biosensors. The specific functionalization of the chalcogenide waveguides and the multivariate analysis of the spectral measurements will make it possible to increase the sensitivity of the probes and make them selective regarding the different types of spores and to discriminate any other element detected (pollen, dust for example). We are thus currently interested in the functionalization of activated GeSeTe thin layers with monosilylated functional groups. The advantage of sol-gel chemistry is that it allows multi-functionalization in a single step. In the context of spore detection, which generally involves several sites, the immobilization of several functions is therefore be studied.

articleTitle: Controlling the transmission bandwidth of anti-resonant hollow-core fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We have developed an innovative anti-resonant hollow-core fiber design with capillaries of alternating thicknesses. This unique arrangement, featuring six silica capillaries of two different thicknesses, effectively narrows the transmission bandwidth while maintaining low attenuation. Validated through simulations, our design marks a significant step in developing the first in-line hollow-core bandwidth filter fiber. We envision that our novel fiber design has a variety of applications, such as suppressing non-linear effects and developing wavelength-selective components for future conventional and quantum communication networks.

articleTitle: Limits to determination of polarization independence in SOAs
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Polarization independence is an important property in some applications of the semiconductor optical amplifier, in particular when amplifying polarization multiplexed signals. The accurate determination of polarization dependent gain (PDG) is far more complicated than the determination of polarization dependent loss in passive components, due to the presence of amplified spontaneous emission and the danger of round-trip reflections. We will discuss factors limiting precise measurement of PDG.

articleTitle: Cross Domain Orchestration and Management of Optical Links in Terrestrial-Non Terrestrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this contribution, we describe different levels of orchestration and management to be adopted in a cross domain Terrestrial and Non Terrestrial Network exploiting the most recent architectures defined for the Core Network since we propose to extend the control of the optical fiber links also to the ones operating in Non Terrestrial Networks, and mainly based on Free Space Optics (FSO). In particular, the NETCONF protocol is proposed for the Southbound interfaces.

articleTitle: Transparent Reflective Metasurfaces: from RIS to near-eye displays
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Transparent reflective metasurfaces offer a flexible paradigm for controlling electromagnetic waves. This paper explores the design and application of transparent metasurfaces across a broad spectrum, from microwaves to visible light. We take advantage of three examples involving engineered geometries and reconfigurable materials to achieve distinct functionalities, such as beam shaping and steering, modulation, and selective color reflection. These results highlight the potential of transparent reflective metasurfaces for dynamic and intelligent control of electromagnetic wave properties.

articleTitle: All-silicon optical modulators and detectors
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Optical modulators and detectors are essential components for photonic circuits serving a range of different applications. Silicon based devices that can be formed using CMOS compatible processing allow the potential for high-volume and low-cost chip manufacturing. Here our recent progress in both silicon based optical modulators and detectors is presented, including a universal component that can serve both functionalities.

articleTitle: A Weak-FBG Sensor Demodulation System Based on a DBR-SOA Tunable Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Compared with a conventional Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG), a Weak Fiber Bragg Grating (WFBG) sensor system can achieve comprehensive and distributed monitoring of various physical parameters. A WFBG demodulation system based on a Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) - Semiconductor Optical Amplifier (SOA) tunable laser is innovatively designed and thoroughly evaluated in this study. This system exploits the unique characteristics of a DBR laser with an integrated SOA to achieve precise tuning of output wavelengths and optical power. The chip-level integrated SOA acts as an optical modulator for ns-level optical pulses generation. This study has paved a way towards a compact, low power consumption, and cost-effective novel equipment for the distributed fiber optic sensing.

articleTitle: Correlated images by using two scattering -Scanning near optical microscopy techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The far field sub-diffraction limited resolution has been achieved by a few imaging techniques, such as: stimulated emission depletion (STED) microscopy, photo-activated localization microscopy (PALM) and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM). All these techniques require fluorescent labels, and the main disadvantages of fluorescent microscopy techniques are the connection between laser wavelength and fluorescent marker and difficulty to attach the marker to the interesting region of the samples. Moreover they may not attach to correct molecule or functional group of interest that create problems in interpreting images. Scanning near field optical microscopy (SNOM) techniques are able to give information at nanoscale in the absence of fluorescent markers.For investigations we used a multimodal system developed by us [1–2]. The system is upgraded with two scattering-SNOM working together with an atomic force microscope (AFM). To image the near field signal by using a scattering -SNOM, we used a laser diode emitting at 638 nm. A pseudo-heterodyne detection scheme was used. In this way we can have a nanoscale optical imaging correlated with the surface sample topography imaging. In the second case we use an inverted microscope integrated in the multimodal system. The beam from the Chameleon Vision II (Ti:Sapphire laser), having 100 fs pulses (coherent) coming from the back side of the sample is focused by using the objective of the confocal system (Nikon) on the sample surface and optical signal from the sample is collected through the detection way of the s-SNOM module. The AFM probe which gives the system resolution was a Ti-Pt coated Silicon probe having a radius of curvature in the tip of only 30 nm, resonant frequency 60 kHz and force constant 3 N/m. The electric field of the laser beam oscillates in a perpendicular plane on the sample surface, parallel with AFM tip axes. It excites the electric dipole placed in the top of the tip which generates a very strong electric field modulated by the electric field of the dipoles placed on the sample surface and also by the AFM tip. This radiation is collected by the objective of the s-SNOM module, placed above the sample and being sent to the detector. The images obtained by the two techniques on the different samples will be presented.

articleTitle: Design, Growth, and Characterization of Semiconductor Optical Amplifier Structures with Wide Spectral Bandwidth in C+L Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this article, we present two designs of semiconductor optical amplifiers intended for amplification in the C and L bands of fiber-optic telecommunications. The active layers consist of strained quantum wells under compression to ensure strong TE mode. The designs are engineered to generate gain over a wide bandwidth through emission associated with the main electronic transitions $\mathrm{e}_{1}-\mathrm{hh}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{e}_{2}-\mathrm{hh} \mathrm{h}_{2}$. We outline the fabrication processes as well as the optical characterizations of two components consisting of 11 and 14 nm thick quantum well active layers. The bandwidths determined in amplified spontaneous emission measurements exhibit broadband characteristics, especially for the design with larger quantum wells. The gain reaches values of 25 and 34.8 dB, with associated bandwidths of at least 71 and 90 nm, respectively. Lastly, the low beam divergence determined in far-field measurements confirms excellent potential for coupling with optical fiber.

articleTitle: Energy level population dynamics in terbium doped chalcogenide selenide glass fibre under pulsed pumping
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Chalcogenide selenide glass fibres have been demonstrated to be well suited for realising lasers operating beyond 5000 nm wavelength with output powers exceeding 100 mW in CW. These devices have many potential commercial applications because they can be in principle tuned over a wide range of wavelengths and can also be potentially made to generate short optical pulses. Therefore in this paper we use a numerical model to study the energy level population dynamics in terbium doped chalcogenide selenide glass fibre under pulsed pumping. The results obtained further the understanding of major dynamic processes governing a mid-infrared pulse generation by a chalcogenide selenide glass host.

articleTitle: A tunable Fabry-Pérot microcavity enables systematic investigation of strong light-matter coupling and energy transfer at distances of several μm
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Cavity polaritons are formed when an optical mode of a microcavity couples strongly to an optical transition such that reversible energy exchange is possible. These hybrid light-matter states exhibit properties possessed neither by the original optical transition or the optical mode, which can result in significant changes to certain material properties. If several different molecules (a donor and an acceptor) are coupled to the same optical mode of a microcavity, the resulting hybridisation has been shown to enable energy transfer at much larger distances than conceivable via dipole-dipole interactions (Förster) or electronic exchange (Dexter), which are inherently short-ranged. For the measurements we will present at this conference, we used two different Jaggregates (organic dye molecules with favourable optical properties due to supramolecular self-organisation) as energy donor and acceptor, respectively, and put them into a tunable Fabry-Pérot resonator, which we operated at mirror distances of several μm. Transmission spectra show the expected splitting of the absorption peaks, indicating polariton formation. Fluorescence measurements suggest efficient energy transfer from the donor to the acceptor molecules at distances of several μm.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Dual-Wavelength 1 μm -2 μm All-Optical Switching Based on All-Solid Dual-Core Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This study focuses on optimizing a dual-core fiber (DCF) structure for femtosecond nonlinear dual-wavelength switching applications, previously demonstrated in the C-band. This contribution aims to synchronize control and signal pulses (CP, SP) at 1030 nm and 2000 nm, respectively, thereby proposing improvements to the DCF fabrication process. Our technological approach relies on the utilization of lead-silicate PBG-08 glass as the core and borosilicate UV-710 glass as the cladding material, ensuring a high index contrast, highly nonlinear cross interaction, and advantageous spectral profiles of the DCF. Through the optimization of core parameters such as shape, diameter, and core-to-core distance, we achieved enhancements in CP-SP synchronization, dispersion engineering, and coupling characteristics, while maintaining device compactness with a mere 1 cm length. The optimized DCF features cores with a diameter of $2.4 \mu \mathrm{m}$ and a core-to-core distance of $3.9 \mu \mathrm{m}$. Additionally, we introduced a novel fabrication approach to maintain circular core shapes and mitigate the asymmetry inherent in previously fabricated DCFs. This innovative method represents a significant advancement in DCF fabrication, offering promising prospects for dual-wavelength all-optical switching. The presented numerical results predict a reduction in switching energy and an improvement in switching contrast, with a simultaneous shift of the switching wavelength towards the mid-infrared spectral region.

articleTitle: Power-over-Fiber Integration in 5G Optical Fronthauling based on Multicore Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Power over Fiber (PoF) performance is reviewed for its integration in centralized 5G optical fronthauling with space division deployments (SDM) through multicore fibers (MCF). Latest PoF results and impact on 5G data traffic quality are presented for different testbeds. Novel solutions for monitoring the PoF signal are addressed. Passive Optical Network (PON) integration and convergence in this scenario is also discussed.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser waveguide inscription in linear and nonlinear mid-infrared transparent glasses
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this paper, we report on the fabrication of integrated photonic devices for the mid-infrared spectral range via the femtosecond laser direct-write technique. Utilising this method, the inscription of wavelength-selective fibre-pigtailed directional couplers in synthetic silica glass with ultra-low hydroxide (OH) content is demonstrated. Further, we show that a tailored compositional redesign of zirconium fluoride (ZBLAN) glass enables the fabrication of optical waveguides with record-high numerical aperture and ultra-low propagation losses. Finally, the design and fabrication of nonlinearly coupled waveguide arrays in Gallium Lanthanum Sulphide (GLS) chalcogenide glass is presented and their application as artificial saturable absorbers for mode-locked mid-infrared fibre laser systems is discussed.

articleTitle: Implementation of Time Zone in China to Save Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Of various energy-saving technologies and low-carbon techniques, the time zone is a natural energy-saving technology. Many countries apply the time zone in their daily life. China, as one of largest countries in the world, occupies from 73 E to 135 E across more than four time zones. However, China has not yet adopted the time zone. In this study, we simulate the daylight at morning and evening in Beijing time for winter, spring, summer and autumn in order to determine whether China can adopt the time zone to save energy. The results demonstrate different daylight across China, suggesting that it would be the best to implement four time zones in China to save the energy, to improve the people’s health and to promote the economic development.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Magnetooptic Rigorous Coupled Wave Analysis – Application to Nonreciprocal Guiding
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this contribution, we present and discuss two results selected from these problems, with the concentration given to the different special modeling techniques, we have recently developed. First, we have developed a specific numerical technique – magnetooptic 3D MO aperiodic Rigorous coupled-wave analysis (aRCWA), in order to cope successfully with the complexity of wave effects in photonic nonreciprocal (one-way) structures, based on MO effects where unidirectional propagation can appear in the presence of an external magnetic field. We will first report here on a specific extension of the RCWA/aRCWA tool, a fully anisotropic method (including general form of anisotropy of both permittivity and permeability) in three dimensional (3D) case, due to its major application also called magnetooptic RCWA/aRCWA (MORCWA/MOaRCWA). We have then focused on the investigation of the spectral and transmission properties of structures based on InSb/dielectric waveguides at THz frequencies, in particular, on a 3D InSb hybrid Si plasmonic channel guiding structure. Both dispersion diagrams of surface magnetoplasmons, as well as relative spectral transmittances of the forward and backward propagating waves have been provided for this structure, proving the one-way behavior. The method can be easily applied for simulating and designing novel MO (and even fully bi-anisotropic) applications, in more complex novel configurations resembling realistic designs.

articleTitle: Photonics for satellite radars: the SPACEBEAM project
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design analysis, the challenges of the development, and the results of a hybrid photonic-integrated circuit as the core element of a spaceborne RF receiver for a synthetic aperture radar in X-band, developed during the H2020 project SPACEBEAM. The designed system is capable of synthetizing three simultaneous scanning beams on the received signal and performing the frequency down-conversion. The whole photonics-assisted system is designed for space compliance and meets the target application requirements, representing a step forward toward a deeper penetration of photonics in microwave applications for challenging scenarios, like the observation of the Earth from space.

articleTitle: Integrating Optical and Mobile Networks: A Comprehensive End-to-End Simulation Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Communications are crucial in human interactions, the economy, education, and accessing and democratizing various services and information. With a vast physical infrastructure deployed, optical networks have been fundamental in end-to-end broadband communications. They are considered the foundation for future communications in modern society. Next-eneration optical networks are expected to provide broadband services with massive capacity, lower latencies, and improved reliability, supporting various ultra-high bandwidth applications: cloud/edge networking, 8K video services, and digital twins. Optical networks have been playing an increasingly important role in mobile communications. They will be key for 5G/6G networks, given their bandwidth, coverage, synchronization, and low latency requirements. Various technologies are being developed for the convergence of optical-mobile networks to enhance performance, improve energy efficiency, and simplify the network’s design, implementation, and operation. Researchers, vendors, and operators must be able to evaluate these new solutions effectively. They require a robust simulation framework that seamlessly implements the mobile and optical domains and their interactions. As far as we know, no open-source simulator has fulfilled these requirements to date. For this reason, in this paper, we present an optical-mobile unified simulation platform that addresses the convergence of 5G/6G technology and optical networks. This tool enables academia and industry members to test new optical-mobile network architectures and end-to-end (multi-technology domain) algorithms for dynamic resource allocation or restoration, advancing the capabilities and understanding of next-generation network technologies.

articleTitle: Electric and Magnetic Field Sensors Based of Dielectric Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The effect of electric and magnetic field on the optical resonances of electrostrictive and magnetostrictive optical resonators is presented. The electrostrictive or the magnetostrictive effect is the elastic deformation of a solid when subject to an electric or magnetic field. The optical resonator has a spherical shape and a diameter of a few hundred micrometers. The resonator is fabricated using a polymeric matrix made of Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) Plastisol with embedded magnetically polarizable micro-particles. When the optical resonator is exposed to an external electric or magnetic field, the morphology (radius and refractive index) of the resonator is perturbed by the magnetic or electric forces acting on it, leading to a shift of the optical resonances also known as whispering gallery modes (WGM). In this study, the effect of a static and harmonic magnetic and electric field on the optical mode shift is investigated. The optical resonances obtained with the PVC plastisol resonator showed a quality factor of $\sim 10^{6}$. The optical shift in turn is monitored and related to the external effect. Sensors based on this concept will be presented for different applications.

articleTitle: Optical Entropy Maximization Leads to Spatial Beam Self-Cleaning in Multimode GRIN Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We present a direct experimental verification of the increase in entropy that accompanies the beam self-cleaning effect and, more generally, the process of light thermalization of a highly multimode beam, as it undergoes nonlinear propagation in telecom standard graded-index optical fibers.

articleTitle: Tuning of birefringence and thermal coefficient of delay of photonic bandgap hollow-core fiber by surface modes
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Surface modes (SMs) are localized modes of photonic bandgap hollow-core fiber (PBG-HCF) existing in the fine structure of core wall. SMs are often regarded hazardous which give rise higher loss by coupling with the air modes of PBG-HCF. In this paper, we report the method of SM engineering in the tuning of birefringence and thermal coefficient of delay in PBG-HCF with relatively low loss. 7-cell PBG-HCF is designed and fabricated with an anisotropic core wall thickness distribution. Owing to the anti-crossing between air modes and SMs, up to $2.6 \times 10^{-3}$ group birefringence is measured in a transmission window from 1472 nm to 1560 nm where the minimum attenuation is $39 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{km}$. The thermal group delay is characterized and discussed.

articleTitle: Propagation of Optical Signals Encrypted with Spectral Phase Encoding and Signal/Polarisation Shuffling
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)

authors.preferredName: João Pedro de Lima Cassiano Pereira

abstract: Non-intrusive tapping and other threats have underscored the necessity for enhanced security mechanisms in transparent optical networks (TONs). In this work, we explore the application of both intra- and inter-signal cryptography techniques to secure TON signals. The intra-signal approach utilizes spectral phase encoding, while the inter-signal technique relies on shuffling the samples among different signals, including the X - and Y polarisation components of each signal. Computer simulation results suggest that encrypted $448 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ dual polarisation (DP) 16-quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) signals may be properly recovered after $\sim 700 \mathrm{~km}$ of standard single-mode fiber propagation.

articleTitle: Nanooptical Substrates for Resonance-Enhanced Gold Growth
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Metal lines grown by photocatalysis from solution and dissolved by chemical dissolution are a promising technical approach to mimic the growth and pruning of long-range axonal connections in neuromorphic computing architectures. We investigate a metal line growth approach on the surface of a photoactive titanium dioxide layer. In order to achieve a light-stimulus dependent metal growth nanooptical templates with different nanostructured lines are suggested. Nanostructures allow for resonance-enhancement of the illumination as a function of wavelength, incidence angle, and polarization. Periodic grating nanostructures with grating periods of 170 nm to 210 nm in $500-\mu \mathrm{m}$ squares and 20-period triangular arrangements for excitation in the UV are investigated. The resonant optical enhancement is characterized by deposition of an emitter material with the absorption maximum matching the excitation laser at 355 nm and fluorescence in the visible spectrum. Resonance enhancement is demonstrated experimentally for the designed nanooptical substrates. Photocatalytic gold-growth experiments are presented exhibiting enhanced gold growth on the nanostructured regions compared to the unstructured regions.

articleTitle: Irradiance Distribution and Performance Analysis of Vector Vortex Beams in Atmospheric Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Free space optical communication (FSOC) offers secure and high data transmission. However, atmospheric turbulence poses a significant bottleneck for FSOC. These limitations can be effectively addressed with vector vortex beams (VVBs), which leverage phase and polarization singularities, exhibiting resilience to turbulence. Despite this potential, existing studies have not explored the irradiance (intensity) distribution of the VVB in the turbulent channel. This paper derives the irradiance distribution for C-point and V-point beams, which are prominent VVBs known in the literature for their increased resilience to turbulence. Additionally, an in-depth analysis of the bit error rate (BER) performance of VVBs using on-off keying (OOK) modulation has been conducted. We tested the model using a scalar Gaussian beam to validate the obtained results and compared it with the results available in the literature.

articleTitle: Achieving Multiple-Days Stability in a Single-Cavity Dual-Comb laser for Spectroscopic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: A portable ring cavity fiber laser that generates two stable orthogonally polarized vector solitons for over 125 hours. Allan deviation $0.0002319 \mathrm{~Hz} / \mathrm{s}$ and SSB phase noise of $-95 \mathrm{dBc} / \mathrm{Hz}$ for at an offset of 100 Hz.

articleTitle: Enabling Enhanced In-Building Solutions Fronthaul Connectivity: The Role of Mode Division Multiple Access in Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper introduces the application of Mode Division Multiple Access (MDMA) in the context of In-Building Solutions (IBS) for mobile networks. The study showcases the successful generation and selection of light modes which are then efficiently multiplexed and demultiplexed at the Remote Radio Unit (RRU) end. Despite the proven operational capabilities, the findings reveal a decline in signal quality as the distance increases, thus limiting the use of MDMA for longdistance fronthaul applications. The proposed system also simplifies the RRU by centralizing key functionalities at the Central Office (CO), potentially reducing costs and the operational expenses (OPEX/CAPEX) associated with inbuilding solutions and other mobile network deployments. This work extends previous research and paves the way for future studies, particularly in the application of the Power over Fiber (PWoF) approach to reduce RRU complexities further.

articleTitle: Non-invasive Vital Signs Monitoring Based on Optical Fiber Mach-Zehnder Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Vital signs monitoring is a key tool in healthcare. We review our recent research on vital signs monitoring system based on optical fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI). The system can collect the user’s heartbeat and breath signals continuously and remotely to provide big data for health analysis. Our technique is non-invasive, highly sensitive, and immune to electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: A comparative analysis of InGaAs SPADs and SNSPDs in entanglement-based Quantum communications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We present experimental results from a Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) setup based on entanglement, where polarization entangled photon pairs are distributed after narrowband filtering and followed by detection employing polarization-based receivers. A comparative analysis of the performance of InGaAs single photon avalanche detectors (SPADs) and superconducting nanowire single photon detectors (SNSPDs), reveals a notable advantage of SNSPDs for QKD applications. The entangled photon pairs are generated using a Sagnac-based polarization entanglement source, and subsequently split by Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexers (DWDMs). These entangled photon pairs are sent to two polarization-based receivers facilitating the comparison between the detection using InGaAs SPADs and SNSPDs. The results emphasize the superior performance of SNSPDs reflected in an around 80 times higher coincidence rate, therefore tolerating around 8 dB higher attenuation values. For both configurations and all considered attenuation levels, the fidelity and quantum bit error rate (QBER) are well inside the respective bounds for secure key generation. This work provides valuable insights for the optimization of QKD systems.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis of Wideband Transmission in Optical Transport Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: This paper assesses the techno-economic prospects of different wideband transmission configurations to scale capacity in optical transport networks. Detailed optical performance estimation and a simulated network loading according to a given traffic profile and growth rate are executed for the different transmission configurations to realise a meaningful techno-economic comparison. Moreover, simplified cost modelling is utilized where some contributors are assigned a single relative cost. In contrast, the remaining cost contributors, for which there is a higher uncertainty (e.g., immature technology) or variability (e.g., scenario dependency), are the subject of parametric analysis. The simulation results over a reference transport network allow us to gain insight into the specific conditions where each wideband transmission configuration is more cost-effective than the remaining ones.

articleTitle: Is the access network ready for Quantum Key Distribution?
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The access network segment represents the end point for the provision of quantum key distribution (QKD) services, offering secure communication to the end users. Yet the integration of QKD into legacy passive optical networks (PONs) is very challenging due to the high losses of the passive optical distribution network (ODN) and the presence of upstream and downstream classical channels belonging to many coexisting PON standards, which are the source of scattered Raman noise photons. In this study we evaluate the sustainability of discrete variable QKD services in access networks supporting one or more PON standards, evidencing the necessity of ODN architectures able to enhance the QKD performance and facilitate the key-exchange over the legacy PON links.

articleTitle: Heterogeneously integrated laser diodes that are efficient and insensitive to external feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We discuss how the design of heterogeneously integrated laser diodes can be optimized to guarantee high wall-plug efficiency for those lasers as well as make them very insensitive to external (parasitic) reflections. We also provide some experimental results obtained for heterogeneously integrated DFB lasers on silicon. We also introduce an opto-electronic feedback loop that allows to modify the external feedback to give optimum linewidth and side mode rejection.

articleTitle: Nanostructuring wide bandgap semiconductors for light manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Wide bandgap semiconductor materials such as III-nitride (e.g., GaN, InGaN, AlGaN) are highly desirable for photonic and optoelectronic devices operating at visible and ultraviolet frequencies such as light emitter, lasers, metasurfaces etc. They can also be interesting for dynamic and tunable nanophotonics enabled by ultrafast carrier injection or to understand carrier behavior based on optical response. A wide range of optical behavior from modified spontaneous emission, lasing, wavefront control is possible via nanostructuring. However, unlike Si and other III-V semiconductors nanostructuring III nitrides pose special nanofabrication challenges. We will discuss low threshold laser, quantum emitters and metasurfaces and relevant nanofabrication approaches used to fabricate them. Combination of dry and wet chemical etching is used to fabricate InGaN quantum well based nanowire array photonic crystals that exhibit low threshold lasing across a wide spectral range covering nearly the entire photoluminescence band as well as achieving emission profile modification. An additional degree of control in fabrication of III-nitride nanostructures can be achieved either through light assisted or unassisted selective electrochemical etching enabling new functionalities and phenomena. Laser assisted photoelectrochemical etching can used to create precise emission wavelength controllable quantum dots-in-wire suitable for single photon generation. Likewise, selective electrochemical etching of doped III-nitride can be utilized to achieve nanoporosity that can used to provide low refractive index optical cladding behavior with respect to the high index substrate. We will discuss how we can use this approach to create efficient III-nitride nanowire array resonators based metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Parametric Modulation Instability in Dual Polarization Driven Passive Fiber Cavities Induced by Periodic Polarization Rotation
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We investigate theoretically and numerically the generation of parametric modulation instability in a cavity made of a highly birefringence polarization maintaining fiber with periodic rotation of the intracavity light field through a Faraday rotator. We developed a model based on a two couple nonlinear Schrödinger equations describing the propagation of the linearly polarized components along the principal axes of the fiber and boundary conditions accounting for the coupler and the periodic rotation of the polarization state of the intracavity field. Analytical predictions obtained with a linear stability analysis and Floquet theory, are validated by numerical simulations, and generation of new parametric MI branches, with regards to the scalar case, is highlighted.

articleTitle: Miniaturizing plasmonic arrays using extreme dispersion
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Nanoplasmonics allows to enhance Purcell factor due to small mode volumes. Recently, use of diffractive modes, hybridized with plasmonic excitations, has enabled to increase the resonance Q-factors, promising to enhance occurring light-matter interactions. These hybrid modes, known as surface lattice resonances, require nanoparticle array sizes ranging from hundreds of micrometers to millimeters, making them unfeasible for several nanoscale photonic applications. Here, we propose to utilize extreme dispersion to dramatically miniaturize the required array sizes. The group index of the surrounding medium is shown to be directly linked to the array size, allowing up to two-orders-of-magnitude decrease in used dimensions. The increase in dispersion is achieved by utilizing Bragg-reflector waveguides. The work paves way for more efficient and smaller nanoplasmonic devices.

articleTitle: Optimizing Dysprosium-Doped Fiber Lasers for Direct Yellow Emission: A Comprehensive Numerical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In recent years, the potential for achieving efficient yellow emission from fiber lasers has significantly increased, thanks to advancements in blue pump laser diodes and fabrication of high-quality Dysprosium-doped fibers. After presenting a comprehensive overview of different glass matrices used for Dy-doped yellow fiber lasers, showing their limits and benefits, this study focuses on the current leading technology, through a comprehensive numerical analysis and optimization of yellow sources based on ZBLAN Dy-doped fibers. Simulation results provide valuable insights into enhancing the efficiency of these lasers through the careful selection of cavity parameters, such as output mirror reflectivity and active fiber length. The findings highlight the current prospects and challenges associated with Dy-doped fiber lasers, while also anticipating their achievable performance as the fabrication technology of glasses, fibers, and other cavity components matures. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to develop efficient yellow fiber lasers, which hold significant potential for various applications in many fields, such as medicine, spectroscopy, and astronomy.

articleTitle: Optical Waveform Sculpturing of a Frequency Kerr Comb from a Brillouin Laser Cavity with Bichromatic Pumping
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We numerically and experimentally investigate the spectral phase profile of a frequency comb generated by the Kerr effect in a Brillouin fiber laser, architecture of which comprises bichromatic pumping and normal dispersion fiber. By manipulating the spectral properties and exploiting the stability of the comb, we demonstrate the generation of a wide range of temporal intensity profiles at a repetition rate of 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Surface post-modifications of 3D-printed micro/nano-materials
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The responsiveness of many sensitive materials is tied to processes and interactions at their interface with the outer environment. The interface properties are themselves highly dependent on the nature of the surface chemical functions and their spatial arrangement. In this respect, developing a surface modification chemistry of micro/nano-materials will open up new possibilities for designing architectures able to interact at the interface. This review presents pioneering approaches in this research field.

articleTitle: Secure Computation Offloading with ETSI MEC+QKD
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: Many modern applications rely on the ability to offload computation-intensive tasks to edge or cloud infrastructures. While this is clearly beneficial from the point of view of the client, because of the decreased load and system requirements, such an approach entails frequent exchanges with the edge/cloud application, which may include sensitive data. The interconnection of the client and remote infrastructures through a Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) network makes it possible to exchange quantum-secure keys between the peer applications. In this paper we study how to achieve this ambitious goal with applications using the Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) programming model in the context of ETSI MEC and QKD standards, as demonstrated in the national project QUANCOM, funded by the Italian Ministry of University and Research.

articleTitle: Probing Goos-Hänchen shifts in surface nonlinear optics by quantum weak measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: The Goos-Hänchen shifts are tiny deviations, in the incidence plane, from the laws of geometrical optics, which are observed when applying these laws to the central axes of incident and reflected light beams. The axis of the reflected beam does not generally emanate from the surface at the incidence point of the impinging beam (spatial shift) and the angle of the axis of the reflected beam does not generally match exactly the incidence angle (angular shift). In this theoretical work, we show how to exploit pre- and post-selected weak measurements of the light polarization to probe the spatial and angular Goos-Hänchen shifts occurring for paraxial Gaussian beams emitted by a surface nonlinear optical process, such as second-harmonic (SHG) of sum-frequency generation (SFG). Pre- and post-selected weak measurements, which were initially developed to probe foundational issues in quantum mechanics, proved very useful to enhance the minute shifts in linear optics that were undetectable otherwise, through a process called weak-value amplification. We further reveal the usefulness of amplified weak measurements in the context of nonlinear optics.

articleTitle: Photonic WDM Switches for Multi-Band Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: To meet the increasing demand of high capacity low cost and low power challenges of 6G distribution networks, exploiting multi-band optical fiber transmission (MBT) operation from O to L bands is an attractive solution to significantly improve the current optical network capacity. The main challenge for MBT is the lack of mature wideband network components. Especially, MBT optical add/drop multiplexers (MB-OADM) that dynamically route the wideband optical signals and network traffic are key network elements. In this work, we report the assessment of MB-OADM node for metro access and beyond 5G distribution networks. Experimental results show that the MB-OADM based network maintains high optical signal-to-noise ratio(OSNR) values up to 36dB in the C-band and 33 dB in the O-band over 100km across five nodes with 20 km link span in between (total 100 km) without additional optical amplifiers at 25 Gbps. BER results indicated that the architecture supports cascading through nine C -band nodes over 45 km with a 3.8 dB power penalty at 25 Gbps and through five O band nodes with a 2 dB penalty at 25 Gbps.

articleTitle: System-level Simulation of Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM) Transmission through PMMA-POFs with Various Index Profiles
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: In this paper, we present system-level simulation studies in PAM4 modulation using Step Index (SI) POFs, Graded Index (GI) POFs, and Multicore (MC) POFs. Our model exhibits very efficient computation time relative to models that use the finite difference method to compute the power propagation in the fiber. This makes it ideally suited for system-level investigations, where long simulation times can be quite discouraging and a real hindrance to productivity and efficiency.

articleTitle: A purpose-specific design for the next iteration of the Madrid quantum network
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: As the Madrid quantum network, namely MadQCI, evolves, applied knowledge transferable to society should be generated. The general-purpose approach to quantum networking has already been successfully tested in several testbeds in Europe, including MadQCI. Now, this test bed will use a purpose-specific design to embody different architectures, techniques and technologies suitable for different application domains, research lines and stakeholders. Several scenarios and some details of their designs are outlined to exemplify this approach.

articleTitle: Generation of hybrid frequency combs in Kerr cavities by non-Hermitian modulations
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
abstract: We show that the introduction of non-Hermitian modulations in a Kerr optical ring cavity induces a hybridisation of the two known formation mechanisms of solitonic solutions. This blends the properties of anomalous and normal dispersion regimes and allows the stabilisation of new families of frequency combs associated to stable solitons, molecules and patterns. The resultant new scenario greatly diversifies the possible generated frequency combs in Kerr cavities and can wide the application range of frequency combs.

articleTitle: Enabling Cost-Effective Fiber Sensing with Quasi-Coherent Detection for PON Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Conference on Transparent Optical Networks (ICTON)
